Q₁(λ⁰)⊗L(pω_λ) need not be p-bounded, so Lemma 4.2.2 should only be applied to M (source issue). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 4.2.12 — Proposition 4.2.10 when λ is restricted away from i₀
items.statement: If, in setup-M-extension, λ_i is p-restricted for all i ≠ i₀, then the conclusion of Proposition 4.2.10 holds.
items.note: Proof: show that Proj(F₁) → M|_G → Inj(F₀) is nonzero by applying gr₁ (socle filtration), using Lemma 4.2.11 and the claim that the socle filtration of Q₁(λ⁰)⊗L(pω_λ) is gr_k(Q₁(λ⁰))⊗L(pω_λ). Reduce to embedding i₀ via alcove considerations and (4.18), then do cases on ω_λ, ω_θ. The case ω_θ = ε′_{1,i₀}, ω_λ = ε′_{2,i₀} uses the swap involution on L(pω_λ)⊗L(pω_λ) and Λ²-antisymmetry. The alcove case list ('λ_{i₀} ∈ D ⇒ θ_{i₀} ∈ E or F; λ_{i₀} ∈ F ⇒ θ_{i₀} ∈ C, D or G') follows the Table 6 labelling and Ext pattern, not Proposition 4.2.9's face criterion. The display 'L(θ⁰+πω_θ)|_G ≅ L(θ)|_G' in (4.19) should read (L(θ⁰)⊗L(πω_θ))|_G. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.13 — generic Deligne–Lusztig representations have deep constituents
items.statement: Let R be an n-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation of G. Then R̄ is (n−2)-deep, i.e. every σ ∈ JH(R̄) is an (n−2)-deep Serre weight. In particular, for n ≥ 2 the elements of JH(R̄) are p-regular.
items.note: Proof: write R = R_s(μ+η) with μ n-deep; the constituents are F(Tr_{μ+η}(ω,a)) with ω in the triangle s(Σ), whose pairings with coroots are at most 2 (Proposition 2.3.4/2.3.5). Used in §4.1.2 (p-regularity) and in §3.5 (7-genericity). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.2.4 — the setup R = R_s(μ^op + η′), σ^op = F(μ), σ = F(μ^op + s(η′))
items.statement: Let μ ∈ X₁(T) be 6-deep in alcove B and R := R_s(μ^op + η′) (a 6-generic, hence 4-deep, Deligne–Lusztig representation by Lemma 4.2.13). Put σ^op := F(μ) = F(Tr_{μ^op+η}(0, 1)). By Proposition 2.3.5 the unique σ ∈ JH(R̄) with d_gph(σ, σ^op) = 3f is σ := F(μ^op + s(η′)) = F(Tr_{μ^op+η}(s(η′), 0)); write λ := μ^op + s(η′), so σ = F(λ).
items.note: JH(R̄) = F(Tr_{μ^op+η}(s(Σ))) (Proposition 2.3.5 with ν = η′−η). (0,1) and (s(η′),0) are at distance 3 in every embedding, and no other pair in s(Σ₀) is. σ is a lowest-alcove weight of defect 0. The symbol λ is reused here with a new meaning. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.14 — σ occurs once in Inj(σ^op), V_μ|_G and U
items.statement: Let μ ∈ X₁(T) be 6-deep in B, R := R_s(μ^op+η′), σ^op := F(μ), and σ := F(λ) ∈ JH(R̄) the unique constituent at maximal graph distance 3f from σ^op. Then [Inj(σ^op) : σ] = [V_μ|_G : σ] = [U : σ] = [gr_{3f}(V_μ|_G) : σ] = 1, with U as in Theorem 4.2.7(3).
items.note: The equalities for V_μ, U and gr_{3f} follow from Theorem 4.2.7(2). For Inj(σ^op) ≅ Q₁(μ)|_G the paper says 'proved similarly using Theorem 4.2.1'. Check: the only constituent of Q₁(μ) whose restriction contains F(μ^op + root) is its highest-weight constituent L(μ^op + pη′), which occurs once. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 4.2.15 — R̄^σ embeds into U
items.statement: Let μ ∈ X₁(T) be 6-deep in alcove B, R := R_s(μ^op + η′), σ^op := F(μ), σ := F(λ) ∈ JH(R̄) the unique constituent at maximal graph distance, and R^σ an O-lattice in R with irreducible cosocle ≅ σ. Then there is an injection ι : R̄^σ ↪ U (U as in Theorem 4.2.7(3)), unique up to scalar.
items.note: Uniqueness: Hom(Proj(σ), U) is one-dimensional (Lemma 4.2.14). Proof: the unique nonzero map R̄^σ → Inj(σ^op) (4.20) factors through U ↪ Inj(σ^op) (4.21), because σ ∉ JH(coker) (Lemma 4.2.14) and R̄^σ has simple cosocle σ. The image contains the minimal submodule of U containing σ, which has length 9^f = length(R̄^σ) (Theorem 4.2.7(3) and Proposition 4.1.1), so the map is injective. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.16 — Theorem 4.1.9(1)–(4) for lowest-alcove weights of defect zero
items.statement: Let R be a 13-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation of G and σ ∈ JH(R̄) a lowest alcove weight with Def_R(σ) = 0. Then Theorem 4.1.9(1)–(4) hold for (R, σ): d^σ_rad(κ) = d_gph(σ,κ) for all κ ∈ JH(R̄); ℓℓ(R̄^σ) = 3f + 1; Γ_rad(R̄^σ) and Γ(R̄^σ) are predicted by the extension graph with respect to σ; and R̄^σ is rigid.
items.note: Proof: by Remark 4.1.10 it suffices to prove Theorem 4.1.9(3). This follows from Theorem 4.2.7(3), Proposition 4.2.15 (R̄^σ ↪ U) and Proposition 4.1.2: Γ(R̄^σ) is the full subgraph of Γ(U) on the geodesic interval between σ^op and σ, where Γ(U)^op is predicted with respect to σ^op. The step putting a general (R, σ) in the normal form R = R_s(μ^op+η′), σ = F(μ^op + s(η′)) of Proposition 4.2.15 is not written out (source issue). Base case of the induction on defect in §4.3. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Saturated inclusion of O-lattices
items.statement: Let V be a finite-dimensional E-vector space and Λ2 ⊆ Λ1 O-lattices in V. The inclusion Λ2 ⊆ Λ1 is saturated if Λ2 ⊄ ϖΛ1, equivalently if the induced map Λ2/ϖΛ2 → Λ1/ϖΛ1 is nonzero. (For lattices with irreducible cosocle: R^{σ2} ⊆ R^{σ1} is saturated iff the reduction R̄^{σ2} → R̄^{σ1} is nonzero, its image then being Q_{σ1}(σ2).)
items.locator: Implicit; first used in Theorem 4.1.9(5), published p. 79; meaning fixed by Remark 4.3.5, p. 100; used throughout §4.3 and §5.1 (pp. 100–118); also used in Lemma 5.2.2 and Theorem 5.3.5 (pp. 119, 125); not formally defined in the paper (cf. Remark 4.3.5, p. 100)
items.note: The paper never defines 'saturated inclusion' explicitly; the meaning (the standard one of [EGS15, §4]) is forced by Remark 4.3.5 ('there is a unique d ∈ Z such that ϖ^dΛ2 ⊂ Λ1 is a saturated inclusion') and by its uses in Lemmas 4.3.9–4.3.10. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

api.name: normalise_inclusion
api.statement: A unique integral power of varpi normalises an inclusion between two lattice homothety representatives.

api.name: reduction_nonzero
api.statement: Normalisation is equivalent to a nonzero reduction map.

items.name: Remark 4.3.5 — existence of the saturation exponent
items.statement: Let Λ1, Λ2 be O-lattices in a finite-dimensional E-vector space V. There is a unique d ∈ Z such that ϖ^d Λ2 ⊂ Λ1 is a saturated inclusion. If V, Λ1 and Λ2 are obtained by base change from an unramified subfield of E, then ϖ^d is a power of p up to units. Since R, R^{σ1} and R^{σ2} are defined over an unramified extension of Q_p, the integer d of Definition 4.3.4 exists.
items.note: D = min{m : ϖ^mΛ2 ⊆ Λ1}. The p-power statement holds because saturation is preserved by base change along the flat map O' → O (the reduction map becomes the base change of a nonzero map of k'-vector spaces along k' → F). This is why d_sat is measured in powers of p rather than ϖ. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 4.3.4 — saturation distance
items.statement: Let R be a Deligne–Lusztig representation (3-generic, standing in §4.3.1) and σ1, σ2 ∈ JH(R̄). Let R^{σ1} be an O-lattice with irreducible cosocle σ1 and fix a saturated inclusion of lattices R^{σ2} ⊆ R^{σ1} (R^{σ2} with irreducible cosocle σ2). The saturation distance (with respect to R) d_sat(σ1, σ2) is the unique integer d such that p^d R^{σ1} ⊆ R^{σ2} is a saturated inclusion.
items.note: Existence by Remark 4.3.5 (d is a p-exponent, not a ϖ-exponent). Independent of choices because lattices with irreducible cosocle are unique up to homothety. d ≥ 0, and d = 0 iff σ1 = σ2. For arbitrary representatives Λ_i of the homothety classes, d_sat(σ1,σ2) = n(Λ1,Λ2) + n(Λ2,Λ1) with n(Λ,Λ') := min{m ∈ Z : p^mΛ ⊆ Λ'}. Conventions (§4): G = ∏_{ṽ∈S} GL3(k_ṽ) (or GL3(F_q)); R a Deligne–Lusztig representation of G over E (ring of integers O, uniformizer ϖ, residue field F); JH(R̄) the Jordan–Hölder factors of the reduction of any O-lattice; R is residually multiplicity free (2-generic). For σ ∈ JH(R̄), R^σ ⊆ R is the O-lattice with irreducible cosocle σ, unique up to homothety ([EGS15, Lemma 4.1.1]), and R̄^σ := R^σ/ϖR^σ. d^σ_rad(κ) := d^{R̄^σ}_rad(κ) is the unique n with Hom_G(κ, gr^n_rad(R̄^σ)) ≠ 0. d_gph is the distance in the extension graph (Definition 2.1.8); Def_R(σ) is the defect (Definition 2.3.8); f = #J. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

api.name: sat_independent
api.statement: The integer is independent of homothetic choices.

api.name: sat_ramified_base_change
api.statement: Extending coefficients preserves the p-exponent.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.6 — the saturation distance is a metric
items.statement: For R as in §4.3.1, d_sat is a metric on JH(R̄): for σ1, σ2, σ3 ∈ JH(R̄), d_sat(σ1,σ2) ≥ 0 with equality iff σ1 = σ2, d_sat(σ1,σ2) = d_sat(σ2,σ1), and d_sat(σ1,σ3) ≤ d_sat(σ1,σ2) + d_sat(σ2,σ3).
items.note: Stated as 'clear' without proof. Proof: with n as in the note to D14, d_sat = n(Λ1,Λ2)+n(Λ2,Λ1) is symmetric and homothety invariant, n is subadditive (p^aΛ1 ⊆ Λ2 and p^bΛ2 ⊆ Λ3 give p^{a+b}Λ1 ⊆ Λ3), and d_sat = 0 iff Λ1, Λ2 are homothetic iff σ1 = σ2 (their cosocles). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Cosocle distance d^σ_rad
items.statement: For σ, κ ∈ JH(R̄), the cosocle distance from σ to κ is d^σ_rad(κ) := d^{R̄^σ}_rad(κ), the unique integer n with Hom_G(κ, gr^n_rad(R̄^σ)) ≠ 0 (R̄^σ is multiplicity free). A priori it need not be a metric: the inequality of Lemma 4.3.3 may be strict.
items.locator: §4.3.1, opening paragraph and remark after Lemma 4.3.3, published pp. 99–100 (notation from §4.1.2, p. 78)
items.note: The name 'cosocle distance' is introduced on p. 100; the notation d^σ_rad is from §4.1.2. Theorem 4.1.9(1) shows a posteriori that d^σ_rad = d_gph. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Corollary 4.3.1 — graph distance bounds cosocle distance
items.statement: Assume that R̄ is 6-deep (every constituent of R̄ is 6-deep) and σ ∈ JH(R̄). Then d_gph(σ, σ') ≤ d^σ_rad(σ') for all σ' ∈ JH(R̄).
items.note: From Lemma 4.2.6 (for 6-deep weights, d_gph(σ,κ) = 1 iff Ext^1_G(κ,σ) ≠ 0) and Lemma 4.1.3: a constituent in radical layer k+1 is pointed to by one in layer k, so there is a chain σ = σ_0, …, σ_d = σ' of adjacent weights with d = d^σ_rad(σ'). By Lemma 4.2.13 a 13-generic R is 11-deep, so the hypothesis holds throughout §4.3.2–4.3.3. The printed index range '0 ⩽ i ⩽ d − 1' should be 0 ⩽ i ⩽ d (see sourceIssues). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.3.2 — the minimal submodule Q_σ(σ1)
items.statement: Let σ, σ1 ∈ JH(R̄). There is a unique minimal subrepresentation Q_σ(σ1) ⊆ R̄^σ containing σ1 as a Jordan–Hölder factor. Moreover (1) cosoc(Q_σ(σ1)) ≅ σ1; (2) Q_σ(σ1) is the image of any nonzero map R̄^{σ1} → R̄^σ.
items.note: Proof: the image of a nonzero map R̄^{σ1} → R̄^σ has cosocle σ1 and, by multiplicity freeness, maps to zero in R̄^σ/M for every M ∋ σ1. Nonzero maps exist: the reduction of a saturated inclusion R^{σ1} ⊆ R^σ; so Q_σ(σ1) is the image of R^{σ1} in R̄^σ for any saturated R^{σ1} ⊆ R^σ (the form used in Lemmas 4.3.10, 4.3.18, Prop. 4.3.19). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

api.name: minimal_factor
api.statement: Q is contained in every submodule containing sigma1.

api.name: image_normalised
api.statement: The image of a normalised lattice map is Q.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.3 (first part) — layers of Q_σ(σ1)
items.statement: Let σ, σ1 ∈ JH(R̄) and σ2 ∈ JH(Q_σ(σ1)). If n = d^{σ1}_rad(σ2), then Hom_G(σ2, gr^n_rad(Q_σ(σ1))) ≠ 0.
items.note: The surjection R̄^{σ1} ↠ Q_σ(σ1) is strictly compatible with radical filtrations (formation of the cosocle is right exact). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.3.3 (second part) — superadditivity of the cosocle distance
items.statement: Let σ, σ1 ∈ JH(R̄) and σ2 ∈ JH(Q_σ(σ1)). Then d^σ_rad(σ2) ≥ d^σ_rad(σ1) + d^{σ1}_rad(σ2).
items.note: Proof: Q_σ(σ1) ⊆ rad^{d^σ_rad(σ1)}(R̄^σ) (minimality), so the inclusion Q_σ(σ1) ↪ R̄^σ is compatible with the radical filtration on the source and the shifted filtration Fil^k = rad^{k+d^σ_rad(σ1)} on the target; combine with the first part. In particular, if σ2 ≠ σ1 then d^σ_rad(σ2) > d^σ_rad(σ1). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 4.3.7 — adjacent constituents have saturation distance one
items.statement: Let R be a 13-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation and σ1, σ2 ∈ JH(R̄) with d_gph(σ1, σ2) = 1. Then d_sat(σ1, σ2) = 1; i.e. if R^{σ2} ⊆ R^{σ1} is a saturated inclusion then so is pR^{σ1} ⊆ R^{σ2}.
items.note: The 'main global input'. Proof by patching: take τ_S with σ(τ_S) = R and a semisimple 10-generic ρ̄_S (10-genericity from 13-genericity of τ_S by the argument of Prop. 3.4.5) with ℓ(w̃_i^*) ≥ 2 for all i and σ1, σ2 ∈ W^?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) (existence: every vertex and every edge of Σ_0 lies in some Σ_w̃ with ℓ(w̃) ≥ 2, checked against Table 2); a weak minimal patching functor M_∞ (Cor. 3.5.16); base change to R'_∞(τ_S) and descent to the subring S (constr-subring-S). With z_j(σ1) = x_j, z_j(σ2) = x_j for j ≠ 1, z_1(σ2) = y_1 (Lemma 3.6.10) and p^kR_1 ⊆ R_2 ⊆ R_1 saturated, the cokernel C of R_2 + pR_1 ↪ R_1 has no σ2, so x_1y_2⋯y_N kills M'_∞(C) (reduced scheme-theoretic support over S, as in Lemma 3.6.2, using S/pS reduced); symmetrically y_1⋯y_N kills the cokernel of p^kR_1 + pR_2 ↪ R_2. Combining, cancelling p (x_1y_1 = p, p-torsion-freeness) and projecting to M'_∞(σ1) gives y_2²⋯y_N² M'_∞(σ1) ⊆ y_1y_2⋯y_N M'_∞(σ1) if k > 1, impossible since M'_∞(σ1) is free over a power series ring over F[[y_1,…,y_N]] (P02). Every step checked; no error found. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Base-changed patched modules M'_∞ and rings R'_∞(τ_S)
items.statement: For a collection τ_S = (τ_ṽ) of tame types and a subquotient V of a lattice in σ(τ_S): R'_∞(τ_S) := R_∞(τ_S) ⊗̂_{(⊗̂_{ṽ∈S} R^{τ_ṽ}_ṽ)} (⊗̂_{ṽ∈S} R^{τ_ṽ,β̄_ṽ,□}_{𝔐̄_ṽ,ρ̄_ṽ}) and M'_∞(V) := M_∞(V) ⊗̂_{(⊗̂_{ṽ∈S} R^{τ_ṽ}_ṽ)} (⊗̂_{ṽ∈S} R^{τ_ṽ,β̄_ṽ,□}_{𝔐̄_ṽ,ρ̄_ṽ}); R̄'_∞(τ_S) := R'_∞(τ_S)/ϖ. In Proposition 4.3.7 the same base change is written over ⊗̂_ṽ R^□_{ρ̄_ṽ}, for lattices R^{σ_i} and weights σ_i. Properties used: for a lattice R^{σ} ⊂ σ(τ_S), M'_∞(R^σ) is p-torsion-free, maximal Cohen–Macaulay over R'_∞(τ_S) and generically of rank one; M'_∞(σ) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over R̄'_∞(τ_S); M'_∞ is exact on these subquotients.
items.locator: §4.3.1, proof of Proposition 4.3.7, published p. 101; §5.1, published p. 110
items.note: Here R^{τ,β̄,□}_{𝔐̄,ρ̄} is the ring of [LLHLM18, Definition 5.10] (cite-LLHLM18-def-5-10), formally smooth over R^{τ,□}_{ρ̄}, so the base change is exact and preserves the MCM property and cyclicity. Properties follow from Definition 3.5.1(1),(3),(4). The two base rings (R^□ in 4.3.7, R^τ in 5.1) give the same modules because the modules are supported on R^τ. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [LLHLM18, Definition 5.10] — the ring R^{τ,β̄,□}_{𝔐̄,ρ̄} (cited)
items.statement: For a tame type τ, a mod p representation ρ̄ and the Kisin module 𝔐̄ ∈ Y^{η,τ}(F) attached to ρ̄ (Theorem 3.3.12), R^{τ,β̄,□}_{𝔐̄,ρ̄} is the complete local Noetherian O-algebra of [LLHLM18, Definition 5.10] (framed potentially crystalline deformations of type (η,τ) together with an eigenbasis β of the Kisin module lifting β̄). As used here: it is formally smooth over R^{τ,□}_{ρ̄}, and formally smooth over the explicit ring R^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃} (resp. its special fibre over R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃}) of §3.6.1.
items.locator: Recalled in the proof of Proposition 4.3.7, published p. 101, and in §5.1, published p. 110
items.note: Cited, not proved here. The description in parentheses is a gloss of the cited object; only the two formal-smoothness properties are used here. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [LLHLM18, §5.3.2] — formal smoothness over R_N (cited)
items.statement: Let N := Σ_{i∈J}(4 − ℓ(w̃_i^*)) and R_N := ⊗̂_{j=1}^N O[[x_j, y_j]]/(x_j y_j − p). If ℓ(w̃_i^*) > 1 for all i ∈ J, then ⊗̂_{ṽ∈S} R^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄_ṽ,w̃_ṽ} is formally smooth over R_N; hence R'_∞(τ_S) ≅ R_N[[t_1, …, t_k]] for some k.
items.locator: Cited in the proof of Proposition 4.3.7, published p. 101; used again in Lemma 5.1.3, p. 112
items.note: Cited, not proved here. Components of length 4 contribute no factor, length 3 one factor, length 2 two factors, so #W^?(ρ̄_S,τ_S) = 2^N (Table 2). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: The subring S and the primes p_S(σ) (proof of Proposition 4.3.7)
items.statement: Fix an isomorphism R_N[[t_1,…,t_k]] ≅ R'_∞(τ_S) and let S ⊂ R_N[[t_1,…,t_k]] be the subring Z_p[[(x_j,y_j)_{j=1}^N, (t_j)_{j=1}^k]]/(x_jy_j − p)_{j=1}^N. Then R'_∞(τ_S) is finite over S, S/pS is reduced, and every maximal Cohen–Macaulay R'_∞(τ_S)-module is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over S. For σ ∈ W^?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) let p(σ) := (z_j(σ))_{j=1}^N + (ϖ) with z_j(σ) ∈ {x_j, y_j} (the minimal prime of Theorem 3.6.4 / Lemma 3.6.10); then Ann_{R'_∞(τ_S)}(M'_∞(σ)) = p(σ)R'_∞(τ_S) (Prop. 3.6.1(2)), its preimage in S is p_S(σ) = (z_j(σ))_{j=1}^N + (p), and Supp_S M'_∞(σ) = Spec(S/p_S(σ)).
items.note: S is used because S/pS = F_p[[x,y,t]]/(x_jy_j) is reduced while the modules are only p-torsion (not ϖ-torsion) when E/Q_p is ramified; this makes 'generically reduced ⇒ reduced support' work. For σ ∈ JH(R̄) \ W^?(ρ̄_S,τ_S), M'_∞(σ) = 0 and one takes p_S(σ) = S (the paper leaves this implicit and uses p(σ) one sentence before defining it). Relies on [Gro65, Corollaire 5.7.10]. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: [Gro65, Corollaire 5.7.10] — Cohen–Macaulayness under a finite local map (cited)
items.statement: As used: let S → R' be a finite local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings such that the maximal ideal of R' is the only prime of R' above the maximal ideal of S. Then a finitely generated R'-module which is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over R' is maximal Cohen–Macaulay as an S-module.
items.locator: Cited in the proof of Proposition 4.3.7, published p. 101
items.note: Cited, not proved here (EGA IV_2). Depth and dimension of a finite module are the same over S and over R' in this situation; maximality uses dim R' = dim S (finiteness). Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).

items.name: Corollary 4.3.8 — saturation distance is bounded by graph distance
items.statement: Assume that R is 13-generic and σ1, σ2 ∈ JH(R̄). Then d_gph(σ1, σ2) ≥ d_sat(σ1, σ2).
items.note: Induction on d_gph using Prop. 4.3.7 and the triangle inequality (Lemma 4.3.6). The step 'pick κ ∈ JH(R̄) distinct from σ1, σ2 with d_gph(σ1,κ) + d_gph(κ,σ2) = d_gph(σ1,σ2)' needs JH(R̄) ≅ Σ_0^J to be geodesically convex in the extension graph; checked by computer on Σ_0 (graph distances inside Σ_0 equal those in Λ_W × A), and the product structure gives the general case. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.3.9 — adjacent lattices are comparable
items.statement: Assume that R is 13-generic. Let σ1, σ2 ∈ JH(R̄) with d_gph(σ1, σ2) = 1. Fix σ ∈ JH(R̄) and saturated inclusions of lattices R^{σ2} ⊆ R^σ and R^{σ1} ⊆ R^σ. Then either R^{σ2} ⊆ R^{σ1} or R^{σ1} ⊆ R^{σ2}.
items.note: Since d_sat(σ1,σ2) = 1 there is k ∈ Z with p^{k+1}R^{σ1} ⊆ R^{σ2} ⊆ p^kR^{σ1} saturated; saturation of both lattices in R^σ forces k+1 ≥ 0 and −k ≥ 0, so k ∈ {0, −1}. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.3.10 — cosocle distance orients the inclusion
items.statement: Assume that R is 13-generic. Let σ, σ1, σ2 ∈ JH(R̄) and fix saturated inclusions R^{σi} ⊆ R^σ for i = 1, 2. If d^σ_rad(σ2) ≥ d^σ_rad(σ1) and d_gph(σ1, σ2) = 1, then R^{σ2} ⊆ R^{σ1}.
items.note: By Lemma 4.3.9 the lattices are comparable; R^{σ1} ⊆ R^{σ2} would give Q_σ(σ1) ⊆ Q_σ(σ2) and hence d^σ_rad(σ1) > d^σ_rad(σ2) by Lemma 4.3.3. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 4.3.11 — radical strata predicted by the extension graph
items.statement: Assume that R is 2-generic and let σ ∈ JH(R̄). The radical strata of R̄^σ are predicted by the extension graph if d_gph(σ, σ') = d^σ_rad(σ') for all σ' ∈ JH(R̄).
items.note: Compare Definition 4.1.8 (a graph is predicted by the extension graph with respect to σ if it has an edge κ1 → κ2 iff d_gph(κ1,κ2) = 1 and d_gph(σ,κ1) ⩽ d_gph(σ,κ2); for adjacent weights the extension graph being bipartite, this means d_gph(σ,κ2) = d_gph(σ,κ1) + 1). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

api.name: predicted_strata_grade
api.statement: The grade n has exactly the factors at graph distance n.

api.name: strata_to_edges
api.statement: Under 13-genericity, predicted strata imply the predicted radical graph.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.12 — predicted strata give a predicted radical graph
items.statement: Assume that R is 13-generic and σ ∈ JH(R̄). If the radical strata of R̄^σ are predicted by the extension graph, then Γ_rad(R̄^σ) is predicted by the extension graph with respect to σ: it has an edge κ1 → κ2 iff d_gph(κ1, κ2) = 1 and d_gph(σ, κ2) = d_gph(σ, κ1) + 1.
items.note: For adjacent σ_i, σ_{i+1} at distances i, i+1: σ_{i+1} ∈ JH(Q_σ(σ_i)) by Lemma 4.3.10, and Lemma 4.3.3 gives d^{σ_i}_rad(σ_{i+1}) = 1, so σ_i rad-points to σ_{i+1}. Conversely an edge of Γ_rad gives a nonzero Ext^1, hence adjacency by Lemma 4.2.6; that its endpoints lie in consecutive strata (so distances i, i+1) follows from the definition of rad-pointing plus the hypothesis, which the proof leaves implicit. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Equation (4.22) and the opposite weight σ^op
items.statement: Let R be 13-generic (standing assumption of §4.3.2) and σ ∈ JH(R̄). Then max{d_gph(σ, κ) : κ ∈ JH(R̄)} = 3f − Def_R(σ). If Def_R(σ) = 0 there is a unique σ^op ∈ JH(R̄) with d_gph(σ, σ^op) = 3f (maximal graph distance from σ).
items.locator: §4.3.2, equation (4.22) and following sentence, published p. 104
items.note: From Proposition 2.3.5 and the definition of defect: in Σ_0 an outer (obvious) vertex has eccentricity 3 and a unique antipode, an inner vertex has eccentricity 2 (5 vertices at distance 2) — verified by computer. Used implicitly: σ^op has defect 0, (σ^op)^op = σ, and d_gph(σ,κ) + d_gph(κ,σ^op) = 3f for all κ ∈ JH(R̄) when Def_R(σ) = 0. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 4.3.13 — maximally saturated constituent
items.statement: Let R be 13-generic and σ ∈ JH(R̄). σ is maximally saturated in R if: whenever κ ∈ JH(R̄) satisfies d_gph(σ, κ) = 3f − Def_R(σ), then d_sat(σ, κ) = 3f − Def_R(σ). (4.23)
items.note: 3f − Def_R(σ) is the maximal graph distance from σ by (4.22). For Def_R(σ) = 0 the condition reads d_sat(σ, σ^op) = 3f. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

api.name: maximal_sat_all_distances
api.statement: Maximal saturation implies equality of graph and saturation distance to every constituent.

api.name: maximal_sat_defect_zero
api.statement: The unique opposite weight suffices at defect zero.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.14 — maximal saturation forces d_sat = d_gph
items.statement: Let R be 13-generic. A weight σ ∈ JH(R̄) is maximally saturated iff d_gph(σ, κ) = d_sat(σ, κ) for all κ ∈ JH(R̄).
items.note: Every κ lies on a geodesic σ = σ_0, …, σ_D with D = 3f − Def_R(σ) (maximal geodesics from σ all have the same length); then d_sat(σ,σ_D) ≤ d_sat(σ,κ) + d_sat(κ,σ_D) ≤ d_gph(σ,κ) + d_gph(κ,σ_D) = d_gph(σ,σ_D) = d_sat(σ,σ_D) using Cor. 4.3.8, so all are equalities. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.3.15 — radical extension paths give chains of lattices
items.statement: Let R be 13-generic, σ ∈ JH(R̄), d < ℓℓ(R̄^σ) and σ_d ← σ_{d−1} ← ⋯ ← σ_1 ← σ_0 := σ an extension path in Γ_rad(R̄^σ) (so d^σ_rad(σ_i) = i). For each i ∈ {0, …, d} fix a saturated inclusion R^{σ_i} ⊆ R^σ. Then R^{σ_d} ⊆ R^{σ_{d−1}} ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ R^{σ_1} ⊆ R^{σ_0} is a chain of (saturated) inclusions.
items.note: Follows from Lemma 4.3.10; the needed adjacency d_gph(σ_i, σ_{i+1}) = 1 comes from Lemma 4.2.6 (an edge of Γ_rad is a nonzero Ext^1), not stated in the proof. Each inclusion R^{σ_{i+1}} ⊆ R^{σ_i} is saturated because R^{σ_{i+1}} ⊆ R^σ is. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 4.3.16 — maximally saturated weights have predicted radical graph
items.statement: Let R be 13-generic. If σ ∈ JH(R̄) is maximally saturated, then Γ_rad(R̄^σ) is predicted by the extension graph with respect to σ.
items.note: Reduced to prop-4-3-16-strata via Lemma 4.3.12. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 4.3.16 (proof) — maximally saturated weights have predicted radical strata
items.statement: Let R be 13-generic and σ ∈ JH(R̄) maximally saturated. Then d_gph(σ, σ') = d^σ_rad(σ') for all σ' ∈ JH(R̄); i.e. the radical strata of R̄^σ are predicted by the extension graph.
items.note: Proved inside Prop. 4.3.16 and used separately later (Lemma 4.3.18, Prop. 4.3.19, where d^{σ_{d−1}}_rad = d_gph is quoted 'by Propositions 4.3.14 and 4.3.16'). If k = d^σ_rad(σ') > d = d_gph(σ,σ'), take a radical path σ_0 = σ → ⋯ → σ_k = σ' and the first index i with d_gph(σ_0,σ_{i+1}) < i+1 (then = i−1 by bipartiteness); Lemma 4.3.15 and Prop. 4.3.14 give p^{i−1}R^σ ⊆ R^{σ_{i+1}} ⊆ R^{σ_i}, so d_sat(σ_0,σ_i) ≤ i−1, a contradiction. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 4.3.17 — lower-alcove defect-zero weights are maximally saturated
items.statement: Let R be a 13-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation and σ ∈ JH(R̄) a constituent with Def_R(σ) = 0. Assume that σ ≅ F(λ) where λ ∈ X_1(T) is in alcove A (the lowest restricted alcove in every embedding). Then σ is maximally saturated in R, i.e. d_sat(σ, σ^op) = 3f.
items.note: Uses Theorem 4.2.16 (the structure theorem for lowest alcove, defect-zero σ; Prop. 4.1.7), for R^*: this makes Γ_rad(R̄^σ) and Γ_rad(R̄^{σ^op}) predicted. A radical path σ → σ_1 → ⋯ → σ^op and its reverse in R̄^{σ^op} give chains R^{σ^op} ⊇ p^{n_{3f−1}}R^{σ_{3f−1}} ⊇ ⋯ ⊇ p^{n_0}R^σ with n_i = d_sat(σ_i,σ^op) strictly decreasing, so n_0 ≥ 3f; Cor. 4.3.8 gives n_0 ≤ 3f. The paper writes 'maximally saturated in R̄' here for 'in R'. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.3.18 — all defect-zero constituents are maximally saturated
items.statement: Let R be a 13-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation. If σ ∈ JH(R̄) and Def_R(σ) = 0, then σ is maximally saturated.
items.note: From lem-4-3-18-step and Prop. 4.3.17 by induction along adjacent defect-zero weights: the defect-zero part of Σ_0 is the hexagon (ε1+ε2,0)–(ε1,1)–(ε1−ε2,0)–(0,1)–(ε2−ε1,0)–(ε2,1), so the defect-zero constituents form a connected graph containing weights in alcove A in every embedding (all a_i = 0). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.3.18 (proof) — maximal saturation propagates along adjacent defect-zero weights
items.statement: Let R be 13-generic and σ_0, σ_1 ∈ JH(R̄) with Def_R(σ_0) = Def_R(σ_1) = 0, d_gph(σ_0, σ_1) = 1 and σ_0 maximally saturated. Then σ_1 is maximally saturated, i.e. d_sat(σ_1, σ_1^op) = 3f.
items.note: Uses geodesics σ_0 → σ_1 → ⋯ → σ_0^op and σ_0 → ⋯ → σ_1^op → σ_0^op (σ^op is the antipodal map of the hexagon, so σ_1^op is adjacent to σ_0^op), the chains (4.24) from Lemma 4.3.15 in R̄^{σ_0} and R̄^{σ_0^op}, and shows that p^{3f}R^{σ_1} ⊆ pR^{σ_1^op} and pR^{σ_1^op} ⊆ R^{σ_1} are saturated via Lemma 4.3.3 and Cor. 4.3.1 (else d^{σ^op}_rad(σ_1) ≥ 3f+1, resp. d^σ_rad(σ_1^op) ≥ 3f+1). Needs σ_0^op maximally saturated: true because d_sat is symmetric and σ_0 is the unique weight at distance 3f from σ_0^op, although the paper appeals to 'duality' (see sourceIssues). The printed normalisation 'R^{σ_1}, R^{σ_1^op} ⊆ R^{σ^op}' should read '… ⊆ R^σ, R^{σ^op} ⊆ R^σ' (see sourceIssues). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 4.3.19 — every constituent is maximally saturated
items.statement: Let R be a 13-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation. Then every constituent σ ∈ JH(R̄) is maximally saturated in R; equivalently (Prop. 4.3.14) d_sat(σ, κ) = d_gph(σ, κ) for all σ, κ ∈ JH(R̄).
items.note: Induction on δ = Def_R(σ); δ = 0 is Lemma 4.3.18. For σ_d at maximal distance d = 3f − δ: if Def_R(σ_d) < δ use induction and Prop. 4.3.14; otherwise pick σ_{d−1} adjacent to σ_d with Def one less (neighbours of inner vertices are outer; distance d − 1 by bipartiteness), which is maximally saturated by induction; Lemma 4.3.9 gives two cases for R^{σ_d}, R^{σ_{d−1}} ⊆ R^σ, and both lead to contradictions via Lemma 4.3.3, Cor. 4.3.1 and the argument of Prop. 4.3.16. Every step checked. With Props. 4.3.14 and 4.3.16 this finishes the proof of Theorem 4.1.9 on p. 110: (1), (2), (5) directly; (3) because Γ(R̄^σ) is acyclic, has edges only between adjacent weights (Lemma 4.2.6) and contains Γ_rad(R̄^σ); (4) by Remark 4.1.10 (not restated in the proof). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Setting of §5.1 (weak minimal patching functor and a tame type)
items.statement: Standing setting of §5.1: S finite; for ṽ ∈ S, F_ṽ/Q_p unramified of degree f_ṽ, ρ̄_ṽ : G_{F_ṽ} → GL3(F) semisimple, continuous, 10-generic; ρ̄_S|_{I_S} ≅ τ̄_S(s, μ) with s ∈ W, μ ∈ X^*(T); K = ∏_ṽ GL3(O_{F_ṽ}); M_∞ a weak minimal patching functor for ρ̄_S (Def. 3.5.1); τ_S = (τ_ṽ) with each τ_ṽ a 13-generic tame inertial type and R_∞(τ_S) ≠ 0; w̃ = (w̃_ṽ) = (w̃_i)_{i∈J} ∈ Adm^∨(η), w̃_ṽ = w̃(ρ̄_ṽ, τ_ṽ), J = ⊔_ṽ J_ṽ with i = (ṽ, i_ṽ); for σ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_S)), σ(τ_S)^σ is the O-lattice (unique up to homothety) in σ(τ_S) with cosocle σ.
items.note: All lemmas of §5.1 are stated in this setting; after Lemma 5.1.2 the weight σ is also assumed to satisfy (5.1) (hypothesis of Theorem 5.1.1). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Presentation of τ_S through the shape w̃
items.statement: In the setting of §5.1, if R_∞(τ_S) ≠ 0 there is w̃ = (w̃_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S} = (w̃_i)_{i∈J} ∈ Adm^∨(η) such that τ_S ≅ τ_S(s(w^*)^{−1}, μ + s(w̃^*)^{−1}(0)), with lowest alcove presentation (s(w^*)^{−1}, μ + s(w̃^*)^{−1}(0) − η), where w ∈ W is the image of w̃; moreover w̃_ṽ = w̃(ρ̄_ṽ, τ_ṽ).
items.note: By Theorem 3.3.12 and Proposition 3.4.1 (V(ρ̄|_{I}) = R_{s'w̃^*}(μ'+η) for τ with presentation (s',μ')). The sign '+' here is correct; p. 112 later prints '−' (see sourceIssues). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Formal smoothness of R'_∞(τ_S) over the explicit rings
items.statement: In the setting of §5.1, Spf R̄'_∞(τ_S) is formally smooth over Spf(⊗̂_{i∈J} R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄_ṽ,w̃_i}), and Spf R'_∞(τ_S) is formally smooth over Spf(⊗̂_{i∈J} R^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄_ṽ,w̃_i}) if ℓ(w̃_i) > 1 for all i ∈ J (i = (ṽ, i_ṽ)). R̄'_∞(τ_S) (resp. R'_∞(τ_S)) is regarded both as an algebra over ⊗̂_i R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄_ṽ,w̃_i} and over ⊗̂_ṽ R̄^□_{ρ̄_ṽ} (resp. ⊗̂_i R^{expl,∇}, ⊗̂_ṽ R^□_{ρ̄_ṽ}).
items.note: As explained in §3.6.1 (diagram (3.9)); for shapes of length ⩽ 1 only the special-fibre version exists. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Cyclicity is insensitive to the base change M_∞ ↦ M'_∞
items.statement: For any subquotient V of a lattice in σ(τ_S): M'_∞(V) is a cyclic R'_∞(τ_S)-module iff M_∞(V) is a cyclic R_∞(τ_S)-module. Moreover M'_∞(V) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over its support.
items.note: 'Easy to see': the base change is along a formally smooth local map, so the fibre at the closed point is unchanged (Nakayama). MCM: V is a lattice (Definition 3.5.1(1)) or ϖ^∞-torsion, then filtered by weights whose images are MCM of the same dimension (Definition 3.5.1(3)). The paper then works with M'_∞ 'without comment'. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 5.1.1 — freeness of patched lattices with irreducible cosocle
items.statement: In the setting of §5.1, let τ_S be a 13-generic tame type and σ := F(λ) ∈ W^?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) such that for all i ∈ J, λ_{π^{−1}(i)} ∈ X_1(T) is in alcove C_1 if ℓ(w̃_i^*) ⩽ 1 (5.1). Then M_∞(σ(τ_S)^σ) is free of rank one as an R_∞(τ_S)-module.
items.note: Proof (p. 116): Lemma 5.1.7 with V = σ̄(τ_S)^σ gives M_∞(σ̄(τ_S)^σ) cyclic; Nakayama gives M_∞(σ(τ_S)^σ) cyclic; it is nonzero by Theorem 3.5.2; R_∞(τ_S) is a reduced domain (Theorem 3.5.3) and M_∞(σ(τ_S)^σ) is MCM over it (Definition 3.5.1(1), printed '(3)'), hence faithful; a faithful cyclic module is free of rank one. Index convention: component i of λ is π^{−1}(i) because Tr_μ(ω,a) lies in alcove π^{−1}(a) (Prop. 2.1.3(1)). See sourceIssues for genericity bookkeeping of auxiliary types and the identification of quotients across types. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 5.1.2 — patched modules of predicted weights are cyclic
items.statement: If σ ∈ W^?(ρ̄_S), then M_∞(σ) is a cyclic R_∞(τ_S)-module (read: a cyclic R_∞-module; it is an R_∞(τ_S)-module when σ ∈ W^?(ρ̄_S, τ_S)). In fact M_∞(σ) is free of rank one over its scheme-theoretic support Spec(R_∞/Σ_ṽ p(σ_ṽ)R_∞).
items.note: Method of Diamond–Fujiwara [Dia97]: the support is formally smooth (components of R̄^τ_ρ̄ are formally smooth by Theorem 3.5.3, with Prop. 3.6.1(2); the paper cites Theorem 3.5.2), M_∞(σ) is MCM over it (Definition 3.5.1(3)), hence free (P02), and e(M_∞(σ)) = 1 (Theorem 3.5.2) gives rank one. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The quotient R_∞(V)
items.statement: If V is a ϖ-torsion K-module satisfying the hypotheses of Lemma 3.6.2 (a subquotient of a lattice in σ(τ_S)), R_∞(V) := R_∞/I(V), where I(V) := ∩_{σ∈JH(V)} Ann_{R_∞}(M_∞(σ)).
items.note: By Lemma 3.6.2, if M_∞(V) is cyclic then M_∞(V) ≅ R_∞(V); only I(V) is used here. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 5.1.3 — cyclicity when all shapes have length > 1 (base case)
items.statement: Assume that ℓ(w̃_i^*) > 1 for all i ∈ J. Let σ ∈ W^?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) and let V be a nonzero quotient of σ̄(τ_S)^σ. Then M_∞(V) is a cyclic R_∞(τ_S)-module.
items.note: If R'_∞(τ_S) is formally smooth over O, Lemma 5.1.2. Otherwise, with the notation of the proof of Prop. 4.3.7 (printed 'Lemma 4.3.7') and (5.2) #({z_j(σ1)}Δ{z_j(σ2)}) = 2d_gph(σ1,σ2) (Lemma 3.6.10): for each σ1 ∈ W^?(ρ̄_S,τ_S) adjacent to σ, with j_1 the index where z_j(σ1) ≠ z_j(σ), M_1 := M'_∞(σ(τ_S)^{σ1}) equals z_{j_1}(σ)·M, M := M'_∞(σ(τ_S)^σ) (from z_{j_1}(σ)M ⊆ M_1, z_{j_1}(σ1)M_1 ⊆ pM and z_{j_1}(σ)z_{j_1}(σ1) = p; uses Prop. 4.3.7, Theorem 4.1.9 and reduced supports as in Lemma 3.6.2). Since every coordinate j is flipped by some adjacent σ1 (2^N weights ↔ 2^N minimal primes), M'_∞(σ) ≅ M/(ϖ, {z_i(σ)}_i)M, cyclic by Lemma 5.1.2; conclude by Nakayama. Checked in detail. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: ρ̄-centred parametrization σ_(ω,a) and the sets JH(σ̄(τ_S)), W^?(ρ̄_S)
items.statement: For (sω, a) ∈ Λ^μ_W × A let σ_(ω,a) := F(Tr_μ(sω, a)). Then W^?(ρ̄_S) = {σ_(ω,a) : (ω,a) ∈ r(Σ)}, and for w̃ ∈ Adm^∨(η) there is a bijection (w̃^*)^{−1}(Σ) ≅ JH(σ̄(τ_S)), (ω,a) ↦ σ_(ω,a), for the type τ_S attached to w̃ (τ_S ≅ τ(s(w^*)^{−1}, μ + s(w̃^*)^{−1}(0)); the page prints '−'). Hence W^?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) corresponds to r(Σ) ∩ (w̃^*)^{−1}(Σ) = (w̃^*)^{−1}(Σ_{w̃^*}).
items.note: Σ = Σ_0^J (Definition 2.3.2), r flips a, W̃ acts on the first factor through W̃^der (usual action), Σ_w̃ := Σ_0 ∩ w̃(r(Σ_0)) (Remark 2.3.10). Proposition 5.1.8 instead uses τ-centred coordinates (W^?(ρ̄_S,τ_S) ↔ Σ_{w̃^*}). Conventions verified by recomputing Table 2 with ε1 = image of (1,0,0), ε2 = image of (1,1,0), α = (12), β = (23), γ^+ = t_(1,0,−1)(13). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Assumption (5.4) — product decomposition of JH(V)
items.statement: Let σ ∈ W^?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) satisfy (5.1) and V be a nonzero quotient of σ̄(τ_S)^σ. Assume that for each i ∈ J there is a subset Σ_{V,i} ⊆ (w̃_i^*)^{−1}(Σ_0) such that ∏_{i∈J} Σ_{V,i} → JH(V), (ω, a) ↦ σ_(ω,a) = F(Tr_μ(sω, a)) is a bijection (5.4). Σ̄_{V,i} denotes the image of Σ_{V,i} in Λ_W.
items.note: 'All representations we consider below satisfy this assumption.' By Theorem 4.1.9 and Prop. 4.1.1, quotients of σ̄(τ_S)^σ correspond to subsets of JH closed under 'being pointed to', and a product set ∏Σ_{V,i} is admissible iff each Σ_{V,i} is closed towards σ_i in the extension graph. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 5.1.4 — gluing step 1
items.statement: In the setting of (5.4), suppose that for each i ∈ J, either ℓ(w̃_i^*) > 1 or Σ_{V,i} ⊂ {(ω,1), (0,0), (ε1,0), (ε2,0)} for some ω ∈ {0, ε1, ε2}. Then M_∞(V) is a cyclic R_∞(τ_S)-module.
items.note: By (5.1), (ω,1) = σ_i ∈ Σ_{V,i} when ℓ(w̃_i^*) ⩽ 1; enlarge V so that (ω,0) ∈ Σ_{V,i}. Induction on n = #{i : ℓ(w̃_i^*) ⩽ 1 and #Σ̄_{V,i} = 3}. n = 0: a length ⩾ 2 shape w̃' with Σ_{V,i} in its constituent set exists (all cases checked by computer; the printed example needs αβt_1, not βαt_1 — see sourceIssues) and Lemma 5.1.3 is applied to τ'_S = τ_S(s(w')^{−1}, μ + s(w̃')^{−1}(0)). n > 0: quotients V^1, V^2 with Σ_{V,i'} = Σ_{V^1,i'} ∪ Σ_{V^2,i'}, both containing (ω,0), #Σ̄ = 2, and V^3 with Σ_{V^3,i} = Σ_{V^1,i} ∩ Σ_{V^2,i}; then gluing-fibre-product with I_1 + I_2 = I_3 from Theorem 3.6.4, Table 3 and Lemmas 3.6.12, 3.6.16(3.19) (Figure 3). The case ω = ε2 on a component of shape α needs w_{ε2} = (c_11, c_32c^*_21 − d_22c_31) from Table 3 (continued) rather than the cited lemmas; verified. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Gluing via fibre products (proof of Lemma 5.1.4)
items.statement: Let V be multiplicity free with quotients V^1, V^2 and a common quotient V^3 of both such that JH(V) = JH(V^1) ∪ JH(V^2) and JH(V^3) = JH(V^1) ∩ JH(V^2). Then V → V^1 ⊕ V^2 is injective with image V^1 ×_{V^3} V^2, so V ≅ V^1 ×_{V^3} V^2 and M'_∞(V) ≅ M'_∞(V^1) ×_{M'_∞(V^3)} M'_∞(V^2). If each M'_∞(V^j) is cyclic with annihilator I_j (so M'_∞(V^j) ≅ R'_∞(τ_S)/I_j by Lemma 3.6.2) and I_1 + I_2 = I_3, then M'_∞(V) ≅ R'_∞(τ_S)/I_1 ×_{R'_∞(τ_S)/(I_1+I_2)} R'_∞(τ_S)/I_2 ≅ R'_∞(τ_S)/(I_1 ∩ I_2); in particular M'_∞(V) is cyclic.
items.note: Injectivity: the two kernels are submodules with no common constituent. Lengths: len(V^1 ×_{V^3} V^2) = len V^1 + len V^2 − len V^3 = #JH(V). The last isomorphism is the ring identity R/I_1 ×_{R/(I_1+I_2)} R/I_2 ≅ R/(I_1 ∩ I_2). The generators can be matched after multiplying by units, since R'_∞(τ_S)/I_3 is local. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 5.1.5 — gluing step 2
items.statement: In the setting of (5.4), suppose that for all i ∈ J, either ℓ(w̃_i^*) > 1 or Σ_{V,i} ⊂ (w̃_i^*)^{−1}(Σ_0 \ {(ν1,0), (ν2,1), (ν3,0)}), where (ν1, ν2, ν3) is (ε1−ε2, ε1, ε1+ε2), (ε2−ε1, ε2, ε1+ε2), or (ε1−ε2, 0, ε2−ε1). Then M_∞(V) is a cyclic R_∞(τ_S)-module.
items.note: #(Σ_{V,i} ∩ r(Σ_0)) ⩽ 5; induction on n = #{i : #(Σ_{V,i} ∩ r(Σ_0)) = 5}. Using eq-5-5 one may change the type so that each i has ℓ(w̃_i^*) > 1 or #((w̃_i^*)^{−1}(Σ_0 \ T) ∩ r(Σ_0)) = 5 ('there is still a surjection σ̄(τ_S)^σ ↠ V by (5.5) and Theorem 4.1.9'). n = 0: V has a quotient V' of the form in Lemma 5.1.4 with M_∞(V) ≅ M_∞(V') (checked by computer). n > 0: #Σ_{V,i'} = 6; the quotient V^1 drops the sink (w̃^*_{i'})^{−1}(ν4,1), and a submodule V^2 with #Σ_{V^2,i'} = #(Σ_{V^2,i'} ∩ r(Σ_0)) = 2 contains it; conclude with [EGS15, Lemma 10.1.13] for M'' = ker(M_∞(V) ↠ M_∞(V^1)) ⊊ M' = M_∞(V^2) (Figure 4). See sourceIssues for the cosocle of V^2, which violates (5.1). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Equation (5.5) — replacing a short shape by an adjacent one
items.statement: Let i ∈ J with ℓ(w̃_i^*) ⩽ 1 and T = {(ν1,0), (ν2,1), (ν3,0)} one of the three triples of Lemma 5.1.5. There is a unique w̃'_i ∈ Adm(2,1,0) such that (w̃_i^*)^{−1}(Σ_0 \ T) = (w̃_i^*)^{−1}(Σ_0) ∩ (w̃'_i)^{−1}(Σ_0) (5.5). If #((w̃_i^*)^{−1}(Σ_0 \ T) ∩ r(Σ_0)) ⩽ 4, then ℓ(w̃_i^*) > 1 or ℓ(w̃'_i) > 1.
items.note: Checked by computer for w̃^*_i ∈ {id, α, β, γ^+} (mod t_1): w̃'_i is unique; when the count is 4 it has length 2 (e.g. α ↦ βα or γ^+α), and when it is 5 it has length ⩽ 1. Note that α ↦ γ^+α changes the translation part by a vector of spread 2 (see the genericity issue). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [EGS15, Lemma 10.1.13] — cyclicity from a cyclic submodule and a cyclic quotient (cited)
items.statement: Let R be a local ring and M'' ⊊ M' ⊆ M be R-modules such that M' and M/M'' are both cyclic. Then M is cyclic.
items.locator: Cited in the proof of Lemma 5.1.5, published p. 115; [EGS15, Lemma 10.1.13] (arXiv:1305.1594, pp. 63–64)
items.note: Cited, not proved here. EGS15's proof: lift a generator m of M/M''; some rm generates M'/M'' ≠ 0, hence generates M' by Nakayama (M'' ⊊ M'), so M'' ⊆ M' ⊆ Rm and M = Rm. Applied with M = M_∞(V), M'' = ker(M_∞(V) ↠ M_∞(V^1)), M' = M_∞(V^2). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 5.1.6 — gluing step 3
items.statement: In the setting of (5.4), suppose that for all i ∈ J, either ℓ(w̃_i^*) > 1 (printed ℓ(w̃_i)) or Σ_{V,i} ⊂ (w̃_i^*)^{−1}(Σ_0 \ {(ν,0)}) where ν is ε1−ε2, ε2−ε1, or ε1+ε2. Then M_∞(V) is a cyclic R_∞(τ_S)-module.
items.note: Induction on n = #{i : ℓ(w̃_i^*) ⩽ 1 and Σ_{V,i} ⊄ (w̃_i^*)^{−1}(Σ_0 \ T) for all three T of Lemma 5.1.5}; n = 0 is Lemma 5.1.5. For n > 0 one may take Σ_{V,i'} = (w̃^*_{i'})^{−1}(Σ_0 \ {(ε1+ε2,0)}), so σ_{i'} = (w̃^*_{i'})^{−1}(0,1), and split into quotients V^1, V^2 with Σ_{V^1,i'} ⊂ (w̃^*_{i'})^{−1}(Σ_0 \ {(ε1−ε2,0),(ε1,1),(ε1+ε2,0)}), Σ_{V^2,i'} ⊂ (w̃^*_{i'})^{−1}(Σ_0 \ {(ε2−ε1,0),(ε2,1),(ε1+ε2,0)}) (Figure 5), gluing as in Lemma 5.1.4 with Theorem 3.6.4 and Lemmas 3.6.14, 3.6.16(3.17), 3.6.16(3.18) (β, γ symmetric, Remark 3.6.5). Ideal relations verified by computer. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark after Lemma 5.1.6 — the condition for short shapes
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 5.1.6, when ℓ(w̃_i^*) ⩽ 1 (printed ℓ(w̃_i) ⩽ 1), the condition Σ_{V,i} ⊂ (w̃_i^*)^{−1}(Σ_0 \ {(ν,0)}) for some ν ∈ {ε1−ε2, ε2−ε1, ε1+ε2} is equivalent to #Σ_{V,i} < 9.
items.note: By (5.1) σ_i = (w̃_i^*)^{−1}(ω,1) with ω ∈ {0,ε1,ε2} is outer; its unique antipode is (w̃_i^*)^{−1}(ν,0) and every vertex lies on a geodesic to it, so a proper subset closed towards σ_i omits the antipode. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 5.1.7 — gluing step 4 (general case)
items.statement: With V as described before Lemma 5.1.4 (σ ∈ W^?(ρ̄_S,τ_S) satisfying (5.1), V a nonzero quotient of σ̄(τ_S)^σ satisfying (5.4)), M_∞(V) is a cyclic R_∞(τ_S)-module.
items.note: Induction on n = #{i : ℓ(w̃_i^*) ⩽ 1 and #Σ_{V,i} = 9}; n = 0 is Lemma 5.1.6. For n > 0 remove the antipode (w̃^*_{i'})^{−1}(ν,0) to get V^1; if M_∞(V) → M_∞(V^1) is not an isomorphism, a submodule V^2 with #Σ_{V^2,i'} = #(Σ_{V^2,i'} ∩ r(Σ_0)) = 2 containing (w̃^*_{i'})^{−1}(ν,0) exists, and 'one argues as in the proof of Lemma 5.1.5' (Figure 7). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Proposition 5.1.8 — the hypothesis (5.1) is necessary
items.statement: In the setting of §5.1, let τ_S be a 13-generic tame type and σ := F(λ) ∈ W^?(ρ̄_S, τ_S). Assume that for some i ∈ J, λ_{π^{−1}(i)} ∈ X_1(T) is in alcove C_0 and ℓ(w̃_i^*) ⩽ 1 (5.6). Then M_∞(σ(τ_S)^σ) is not free as an R_∞(τ_S)-module.
items.note: Only sketched and not used later. Sketch (τ-centred coordinates): σ' ∈ W^?(ρ̄_S,τ_S) adjacent to σ at each i satisfying (5.6), with (5.1); ι : σ(τ_S)^σ ↪ σ(τ_S)^{σ'} saturated identifies M_∞(σ(τ_S)^σ) with an ideal I(C) of R_∞(τ_S) ≅ M_∞(σ(τ_S)^{σ'}); I(C)R̄_∞ = I(V)R̄_∞ for V = coker(ι mod ϖ), whose predicted constituents are Σ_{w̃^*} \ ∏_i Σ_{V^c,i} (lists checked by computer); I(V) comes from I = ⊗̂_i ∩_{Σ_{w̃_i^*} \ Σ_{V^c,i}} c_(ν_i,c_i) (radical by radical-tensor-product), and the minimal number of generators is ∏_i dim(∩ c ⊗ F). Computer check: for ℓ(w̃_i^*) = 0 each factor needs 2 generators (sketch works); for ℓ(w̃_i^*) = 1 each factor is principal, so the sketch fails there, although a complementary-ideal argument appears to rescue the statement — see sourceIssues. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Radical ideals in (completed) tensor products (proof of Prop. 5.1.8)
items.statement: Let R, S be reduced local Noetherian rings over a perfect field k, and J ⊆ R, L ⊆ S radical ideals. Then J ⊗_k L is a radical ideal of R ⊗_k S, because (R ⊗_k S)/(J ⊗_k L) embeds into ((R/J) ⊗_k S) × (R ⊗_k (S/L)), which is reduced. In the situation of Proposition 5.1.8 (complete local F-algebras), being radical is preserved by completion, so J ⊗̂_k L is radical in R ⊗̂_k S.
items.locator: §5.1, proof of Proposition 5.1.8, published p. 118; also §5.1, proof of Proposition 5.1.8 (continued from p. 117), published p. 118
items.note: J ⊗ L = (J ⊗ S) ∩ (R ⊗ L) (choose bases of J, L and extend them to bases of R, S); tensor products of reduced algebras over a perfect field are reduced. The completion step is asserted without detail; it holds for complete local Noetherian F-algebras. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).

items.name: Nakayama's lemma (as used for cyclicity)
items.statement: Let (A, m) be a local ring, I ⊆ m an ideal and M a finitely generated A-module. If N ⊆ M is a finitely generated submodule with N ⊆ IN, then N = 0. Consequently, if M/IM is cyclic (e.g. I = (ϖ) or I = (ϖ, z_1(σ), …, z_N(σ))) then M is cyclic; and the minimal number of generators of M is dim_{A/m}(M/mM).
items.locator: Used in the proofs of Lemma 5.1.3 (p. 112), Theorem 5.1.1 (p. 116), Proposition 5.1.8 (p. 118), and in [EGS15, Lemma 10.1.13]
items.note: Standard. Library: Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot at the pinned commits.

items.name: MCM modules over regular local rings are free (Auslander–Buchsbaum–Serre)
items.statement: Let A be a regular local ring and M a nonzero finitely generated maximal Cohen–Macaulay A-module (depth M = dim A). Then M is free: pd_A M < ∞ (Auslander–Buchsbaum–Serre) and pd_A M = depth A − depth M = 0 (Auslander–Buchsbaum formula). If moreover the multiplicity e(M) equals 1, then M ≅ A.
items.locator: Used in Lemma 5.1.2 (p. 111) and at the end of the proof of Proposition 4.3.7 (p. 102); also general; implicit in Lemma 5.2.2 ('locally free … since they are Cohen–Macaulay of full support over the regular scheme U'), published p. 119, and in Lemma 5.1.2
items.note: Standard. In Prop. 4.3.7 applied to M'_∞(σ1) over the regular ring S/p_S(σ1) ≅ F_p[[y_1,…,y_N,t_1,…,t_k]] (only freeness is used); in Lemma 5.1.2 to M_∞(σ) over its formally smooth support, with e(M_∞(σ)) = 1 from Theorem 3.5.2. Planned: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3 plans depth, Cohen–Macaulay modules and Auslander–Buchsbaum.

items.name: §5.2 setup — the crossing locus Z and its complement U ⊂ X∞(τ_𝒮)
items.statement: Setting of §5.2: 𝒮, ρ̄_𝒮 = (ρ̄_ṽ)_{ṽ∈𝒮} (each ρ̄_ṽ : G_{F_ṽ} → GL₃(𝔽) semisimple and 10-generic, F_ṽ/ℚ_p finite unramified), R∞, X∞ and a weak minimal patching functor M∞ for ρ̄_𝒮 are as in §5.1; τ_𝒮 = (τ_ṽ)_{ṽ∈𝒮} with each τ_ṽ a 13-generic tame inertial type. Put X∞(τ_𝒮) := Spec R∞(τ_𝒮), where R∞(τ_𝒮) = (⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}) ⊗̂_{(⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^□)} R∞. Let Z ⊂ X∞(τ_𝒮) be the locus of points lying on two irreducible components of the special fibre X∞(τ_𝒮) ⊗_𝒪 𝔽, and let j : U := X∞(τ_𝒮) \ Z ↪ X∞(τ_𝒮) be the natural open immersion. The paper asserts: the codimension of Z ⊂ X∞(τ_𝒮) is two.
items.note: Z is the union of the pairwise intersections of the finitely many irreducible components of the special fibre, hence closed and of the form V(I) with I finitely generated, so U is quasi-compact and j_* preserves quasi-coherence. What is true and used is codim ≥ 2: the special fibre is equidimensional of dimension d (dim X∞(τ_𝒮) = d+1), a point on two distinct components has codimension ≥ 1 in the special fibre, and ϖ lies in it. Z may be empty (special fibre irreducible, i.e. #W?(ρ̄_𝒮,τ_𝒮) = 1). In §3.5, X∞(τ_𝒮) denotes Spf; here it is redefined as the spectrum of the complete local ring. Previous-pass statement ('every point has height ≥ 2; may be empty') kept in this note; the item now records the definitions as printed. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

api.name: regular_complement
api.statement: U is regular.

api.name: gauge_base
api.statement: j is pulled back from the local deformation base.

items.name: X∞(τ_𝒮) is normal and Cohen–Macaulay
items.statement: In the setting of D20, X∞(τ_𝒮) = Spec R∞(τ_𝒮) is a normal and Cohen–Macaulay scheme.
items.note: Asserted 'by (the proof of) Theorem 3.5.3': each R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ} is a normal Cohen–Macaulay domain with reduced special fibre whose components are formally smooth, and R∞(τ_𝒮) ≅ (⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ})[[x₁,…,x_h]]; the completed tensor product needs the proof, not only the statement, of Theorem 3.5.3. Consequence used implicitly in Theorem 5.2.3: R∞(τ_𝒮) is a local normal ring, hence a domain (when nonzero), so a cyclic module of full support is free of rank one, and R∞(τ_𝒮) = Γ(U, 𝒪_U) (depth ≥ 2 along Z). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: U and j are pulled back from the local deformation space
items.statement: Let U₀ ⊂ Spf(⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}) be defined in the same way as U (complement of the locus of points lying on two irreducible components of the special fibre) and j₀ : U₀ ↪ Spf(⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}) the open immersion. Then j and U are obtained by pulling back j₀ and U₀ along the formally smooth map X∞(τ_𝒮) → Spf(⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}).
items.note: Stated without proof ('Note that'). Justification: the map is R∞(τ_𝒮) ≅ (⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ})[[x₁,…,x_h]] (formally smooth, same residue field), and T62 shows that the minimal primes of the special fibre extend and the crossing locus pulls back. 'Spf' is used for the underlying ordinary spectrum as a point set; j_{0*}, j₀^* are taken on Spec(⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 5.2.1 — U is regular
items.statement: In the setting of D20, the scheme U = X∞(τ_𝒮) \ Z is regular.
items.note: Proof as printed (checked): the irreducible components of the special fibre of X∞(τ_𝒮) are formally smooth over 𝔽 and the special fibre is reduced (last part of Theorem 3.5.3), so the special fibre Ū of U (points on exactly one component) is regular; at a characteristic-p point x, dim_k T_xU ≤ dim_k T_xŪ + 1, and by p-flatness dim 𝒪_{U,x} = dim 𝒪_{Ū,x} + 1, so U is regular at x; the generic fibre of U equals that of X∞(τ_𝒮), which is regular (R∞(τ_𝒮)[1/p] regular). Correct. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Notation j^*, j_* on quasi-coherent sheaves
items.statement: j^* : QCoh(X∞(τ_𝒮)) → QCoh(U) is restriction and j_* : QCoh(U) → QCoh(X∞(τ_𝒮)) is pushforward. For an R∞(τ_𝒮)-module M, j_*j^*M̃ is the quasi-coherent sheaf associated with the R∞(τ_𝒮)-module Γ(U, M̃) (D23); for an ideal I ⊂ R∞(τ_𝒮), j_*j^*I is the ideal H_U(I) of D24, and for a submodule N of a module M with j_*j^*M = M, j_*j^*N denotes the corresponding submodule of M.
items.note: The paper uses sheaf and module language interchangeably on the affine scheme X∞(τ_𝒮) (L08). The submodule/ideal interpretation of j_*j^*(·) is implicit in Theorem 5.2.3 and Remark 5.2.4. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The prime ideal p(θ) of a Serre weight θ = ⊗θ_ṽ
items.statement: For θ = ⊗_{ṽ∈𝒮} θ_ṽ ∈ W?(ρ̄_𝒮), p(θ) := Σ_{ṽ∈𝒮} p(θ_ṽ), where p(θ_ṽ) ⊂ R_ṽ^□ is the prime ideal attached to θ_ṽ ∈ W?(ρ̄_ṽ) by Proposition 3.6.1(1) (unique assignment with Spec(R̄_ṽ^{τ}) = ∪_{σ∈W?(ρ̄_ṽ,τ)} Spec(R_ṽ^□/p(σ)) for every tame τ); the sum is formed in ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^□ and extended to R∞ and R∞(τ_𝒮).
items.note: Π ∈ p(θ). By Proposition 3.6.1(2) the scheme-theoretic support of M∞(θ) is Spec(R∞/p(θ)R∞); for θ ∈ W?(ρ̄_𝒮,τ_𝒮) the image of p(θ) in R∞(τ_𝒮) is the height-one prime of the component of the special fibre labelled θ. ∏_θ p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮) is an ordinary product of ideals. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Multiplicity m(θ) of θ in the cokernel of a saturated injection
items.statement: Let σ, κ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮)) and ι : σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ↪ σ(τ_𝒮)^σ a saturated injection of 𝒪-lattices (σ(τ_𝒮)^σ = the lattice, unique up to homothety, with irreducible cosocle σ). For θ ∈ W?(ρ̄_𝒮), m(θ) is the multiplicity with which θ appears (as a Jordan–Hölder factor) in coker ι.
items.note: Coker ι is a K-module of finite length killed by a power of ϖ (ι ⊗ E is an isomorphism). m(θ) = 0 unless θ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮)); σ̄(τ_𝒮) is multiplicity free for 13-generic τ_𝒮, but coker ι can contain θ several times. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 5.2.2 — image of j^*M∞(ι) on the regular locus
items.statement: Let σ, κ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮)) and let ι : σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ↪ σ(τ_𝒮)^σ be a saturated injection. For any θ = ⊗_{ṽ∈𝒮} θ_ṽ ∈ W?(ρ̄_𝒮), let m(θ) be the multiplicity with which θ appears in the cokernel of ι. Then the induced injection j^*M∞(ι) : j^*M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ) ↪ j^*M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ) has image j^*(∏_{θ∈W?(ρ̄_𝒮)} p(θ)^{m(θ)} M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)), where p(θ) = Σ_{ṽ∈𝒮} p(θ_ṽ).
items.note: Proof: both sheaves are locally free of rank one on U (lemma-5-2-2-locally-free); the image is J ⊗_{𝒪_U} j^*M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ) with J the ideal sheaf of the Cartier divisor of the cokernel, and J = j^*(∏ p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮)) (lemma-5-2-2-divisor-ideal, asserted as 'easily seen'); finally J ⊗ j^*M∞(σ^σ) ≅ J·j^*M∞(σ^σ) = j^*(∏ p(θ)^{m(θ)} M∞(σ^σ)) because j^*M∞(σ^σ) is locally free. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Patched lattices are line bundles on U (step in Lemma 5.2.2)
items.statement: j^*(M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)) and j^*(M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)) are locally free of rank one on U, since they are Cohen–Macaulay of full support over the regular scheme U (Definition 3.5.1).
items.note: Definition 3.5.1(1): M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)°) is p-torsion free and maximal Cohen–Macaulay over R∞(τ_𝒮) (a domain, so full support). At x ∈ U the localization has depth = dim 𝒪_{U,x} (T57), hence is free over the regular local ring 𝒪_{U,x} (general-mcm-regular-free). Rank ≤ 1 by Definition 3.5.1(4) and ≥ 1 by full support; so rank one. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The Cartier divisor of coker j^*M∞(ι) (step in Lemma 5.2.2)
items.statement: The image of j^*M∞(ι) is J ⊗_{𝒪_U} j^*(M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)), where J is the ideal sheaf of the Cartier divisor corresponding to the cokernel of j^*M∞(ι), and J = j^*(∏_{θ∈W?(ρ̄_𝒮)} p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮)).
items.note: The second equality is asserted as 'easily seen' (recorded as a gap). Argument: coker(j^*M∞(ι)) = j^*M∞(coker ι) by exactness of M∞, and M∞(coker ι) is filtered by M∞(θ') for θ' ∈ JH(coker ι) with multiplicity; M∞(θ') = 0 unless θ' ∈ W?(ρ̄_𝒮), and then it is supported on Spec(R∞/p(θ')) with e(M∞(θ')) = 1 (Theorem 3.5.2, Proposition 3.6.1(2)), so its length at the generic point of V(p(θ)) is δ_{θθ'}; the divisor is therefore Σ_θ m(θ)[V(p(θ)) ∩ U], and on the regular scheme U each p(θ)𝒪_U is the invertible ideal of a prime divisor (general-cartier-divisor-line-bundles). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 5.2.3 — gauge: the image of M∞(ι) is an ideal times M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)
items.statement: With the notation of Lemma 5.2.2 (σ, κ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮)), ι : σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ↪ σ(τ_𝒮)^σ saturated, m(θ), p(θ)), suppose further that σ is as in Theorem 5.1.1, i.e. σ = F(λ) ∈ W?(ρ̄_𝒮, τ_𝒮) with λ_{π^{-1}(i)} ∈ X₁(T) in alcove C₁ for every i ∈ 𝒥 with ℓ(w̃*_i) ≤ 1 (condition (5.1)). Then the induced injection M∞(ι) : M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ) ↪ M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ) has image j_*j^*(∏_{θ∈W?(ρ̄_𝒮)} p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮)) · M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ).
items.note: Proof: (i) for a maximal Cohen–Macaulay sheaf ℳ on X∞(τ_𝒮), j_*j^*ℳ = ℳ (thm-5-2-3-step-extension, cf. [HK04, Prop. 3.5]); applied to im M∞(ι) ≅ M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ) this and Lemma 5.2.2 give im M∞(ι) = j_*j^*(∏ p(θ)^{m(θ)} M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)); (ii) M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ) is free of rank one over R∞(τ_𝒮) by Theorem 5.1.1, so j_*j^*(I·M) = (j_*j^*I)·M (T61). j_*j^*I is the ideal H_U(I) of D24. The point stressed in §5.3: the image is an ideal times a free module, which is what makes Theorem 5.3.5 work. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Extension across Z for maximal Cohen–Macaulay sheaves (step in Theorem 5.2.3)
items.statement: As printed: 'If ℳ is a Cohen–Macaulay sheaf on X∞(τ_𝒮), then j_*j^*ℳ = ℳ since the codimension of Z is two (cf. [HK04, Proposition 3.5]).' Form actually valid and used: if ℳ is a coherent sheaf on X∞(τ_𝒮) which is Cohen–Macaulay of full support (maximal Cohen–Macaulay over R∞(τ_𝒮)), then the natural map ℳ → j_*j^*ℳ is an isomorphism.
items.note: The printed statement is false for Cohen–Macaulay sheaves supported on a component of the special fibre (recorded as an issue); it is applied only to im M∞(ι) ≅ M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ), which is maximal CM by Definition 3.5.1(1). Proof of the valid form: for P ∈ Z, depth ℳ_P = dim 𝒪_P ≥ 2 (T57), so depth_I(ℳ) ≥ 2 for I with V(I) = Z (T65), hence H⁰_I(ℳ) = H¹_I(ℳ) = 0 (T56) and the exact sequence 0 → H⁰_I(ℳ) → ℳ → Γ(U, ℳ) → H¹_I(ℳ) → 0 gives the claim. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 5.2.4 — the gauge ideal is defined over the local deformation rings
items.statement: As j comes from pulling back j₀ via X∞(τ_𝒮) → Spf(⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}) and the p(θ) are ideals of ⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}, the ideal j_*j^*(∏_{θ∈W?(ρ̄_𝒮)} p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮)) = j_{0*}j₀^*(∏_{θ∈W?(ρ̄_𝒮)} p(θ)^{m(θ)} ⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}) · R∞(τ_𝒮) comes from an ideal in ⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^□.
items.note: The displayed equality is flat base change of sections over the quasi-compact open (T54, T60) along ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ} → R∞(τ_𝒮) = (⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ})[[x₁,…,x_h]], with U the preimage of U₀ (T62). 'Comes from an ideal in ⊗̂R^□' = it is the extension of the preimage in ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^□ of an ideal of the quotient ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}. The ideal depends only on local data (ρ̄_𝒮, τ_𝒮, σ, κ, ι). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Sections of a module over a quasi-compact open of an affine scheme
items.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I = (f₁,…,f_r) ⊂ A, U = Spec A \ V(I), and M an A-module. Define Sec_U(M) := Γ(U, M̃). By the sheaf axiom for the cover U = ∪_i D(f_i), Sec_U(M) is the kernel of ∏_i M_{f_i} → ∏_{i<j} M_{f_if_j}, (m_i)_i ↦ (m_i − m_j)_{i<j} (images in M_{f_if_j}). For r = 0 (U = ∅), Sec_U(M) = 0.
items.locator: general; used as the meaning of j_*j^* in Theorem 5.2.3 and Remark 5.2.4 (published p. 120)
items.note: Used: j_*j^*M̃ on the affine X∞(τ_𝒮) is the sheaf associated with Sec_U(M), U = X∞(τ_𝒮) \ Z. Standard. Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 (route 6).

api.name: sections_restrict
api.statement: Construct the natural restriction M→Sec_U(M).

api.name: sections_change_generators
api.statement: Canonical identification for two finite lists defining the same open U.

api.name: sections_flat_base_change
api.statement: Use T54 for an A-flat algebra B.

items.name: Hartogs closure H_U(J) of an ideal
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring and U ⊂ Spec A a quasi-compact open such that the restriction A → Γ(U, 𝒪_U) is an isomorphism. For an ideal J ⊂ A, H_U(J) is the image of Γ(U, J̃|_U) ↪ Γ(U, 𝒪_U) ≅ A; it is an ideal of A containing J. The embedding into A (not only the isomorphism class of Γ(U, J̃|_U)) is part of the construction.
items.locator: general; this is the ideal j_*j^*(∏ p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮)) of Theorem 5.2.3 and Remark 5.2.4, published p. 120
items.note: Used with A = R∞(τ_𝒮) (normal CM, so A = Γ(U, 𝒪) because codim Z ≥ 2) and A = ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}. Replaces the HK04 citation by a self-contained module-theoretic definition. Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 (route 6).

api.name: ideal_le_hartogs
api.statement: J⊂H_U(J) via restriction.

api.name: hartogs_restrict
api.statement: The associated sheaf of H_U(J) restricts to J-tilde on U; use quasi-coherence of a quasi-compact open pushforward.

api.name: hartogs_flat
api.statement: For flat B, identify H_U(J)B with H_(U_B)(JB) under the induced structure-sheaf isomorphism.

items.name: Torsion-free specialization of a module at an 𝒪-point
items.statement: Let A → 𝒪 be a ring map to a discrete valuation ring and M a finitely generated A-module. Set M_𝒪^{tf} := (M ⊗_A 𝒪)/T, where T is the 𝒪-torsion submodule (elements killed by a nonzero element of 𝒪). In general M_𝒪^{tf} differs from M ⊗_A 𝒪.
items.locator: general; used in the proof of Theorem 5.3.5 ('(the p-torsion-free part of)' before (5.9)), published p. 126
items.note: In the paper A = R∞(τ_𝒮), A → 𝒪 = R∞/λ, M = M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ); the paper writes M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)/λ ≅ 𝒪 where only M_𝒪^{tf} ≅ 𝒪 holds (issue). Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).

api.name: specialize_tf_map
api.statement: An A-linear map induces a map on torsion-free specializations.

api.name: specialize_tf_generic
api.statement: Tensoring M_O^tf with Frac(O) agrees with tensoring M with Frac(O).

api.name: specialize_tf_rank_one
api.statement: Use T63 for a lattice image containing a nonzero power of the coefficient uniformizer.

items.name: Flat base change for sections over a quasi-compact open
items.statement: Let A → B be a flat ring map, U ⊂ Spec A a quasi-compact open, U_B its preimage in Spec B, and M an A-module. Then the natural map Sec_U(M) ⊗_A B → Sec_{U_B}(M ⊗_A B) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: general (degree-zero case of flat base change for quasi-coherent cohomology; Stacks Tag 02KH as given by the earlier checkpoint); used in Remark 5.2.4, published p. 120
items.note: Used for ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ} → R∞(τ_𝒮), which is flat (power series ring). Proof in degree 0: Sec_U(M) is the kernel in D23 and ⊗_A B is exact on it. Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 (route 7).

items.name: Depth ≥ 2 kills H⁰_I and H¹_I
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring, M a finitely generated A-module and I ⊂ A an ideal. If depth_I(M) ≥ 2 then H⁰_I(M) = H¹_I(M) = 0. If IM = M (depth_I(M) = ∞) both groups vanish as well.
items.locator: general; input for [HK04, Prop. 3.5] in the proof of Theorem 5.2.3, published p. 120 (Stacks reference from the earlier checkpoint: Tag 0AVY, not re-verified)
items.note: Standard: H^i_I(M) = 0 for i < depth_I(M). Not stated in the paper; it is the content behind 'j_*j^*ℳ = ℳ'. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).

items.name: Localizations of full-support Cohen–Macaulay modules have full depth
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian local ring and M a finitely generated Cohen–Macaulay A-module with Supp(M) = Spec A. Then for every P ∈ Spec A, M_P is Cohen–Macaulay with depth_{A_P}(M_P) = dim A_P. In particular depth M_P ≥ 2 for every prime P of height ≥ 2.
items.locator: general; used in Lemma 5.2.2 (local freeness on U) and Theorem 5.2.3 (depth along Z), published pp. 119–120 (Stacks Lemma 10.103.11 and Definition 10.103.8 as given by the earlier checkpoint)
items.note: Localization of a CM module is CM, and dim Supp(M_P) = dim A_P when Supp M = Spec A. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).

items.name: The Hartogs closure is a coherent ideal extending J
items.statement: In the situation of D24 (A Noetherian, U quasi-compact, A ≅ Γ(U, 𝒪_U)), H_U(J) is a finitely generated ideal of A whose associated sheaf is j_*(J̃|_U) and which restricts to J̃ on U. If depth_{A_P}(J_P) ≥ 2 for every P ∈ Spec A \ U, then H_U(J) = J.
items.locator: general; the ideal in Theorem 5.2.3 and Remark 5.2.4, published p. 120
items.note: J is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so j_*(J̃|_U) is quasi-coherent and is a subsheaf of j_*𝒪_U = 𝒪_X; the last claim is T56/T65 applied to J. In the paper H_U(∏p(θ)^{m(θ)}) is typically strictly larger than ∏p(θ)^{m(θ)}: this is why the gauge ideal is written with j_*j^*. Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 (route 6).

items.name: Hartogs closure commutes with flat base change
items.statement: Let A → B be a flat map of Noetherian rings, U ⊂ Spec A a quasi-compact open with A ≅ Γ(U, 𝒪_U), and U_B ⊂ Spec B its preimage. Then B ≅ Γ(U_B, 𝒪) canonically, and for every ideal J ⊂ A, H_U(J)·B = H_{U_B}(JB) as ideals of B.
items.note: From T54 applied to M = A and M = J (flatness gives J ⊗_A B = JB). This is the displayed equality of Remark 5.2.4, with A = ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}, B = R∞(τ_𝒮), U = U₀ (and U_B = U by T62). Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 (route 7).

items.name: Hartogs closure times a free module
items.statement: Let A, U be as in D24, J ⊂ A an ideal and L a finite free A-module. Then Γ(U, (JL)~) = H_U(J)·L inside Γ(U, L̃) = L. For L of rank one this is H_U(J)·L and does not depend on the choice of basis.
items.locator: general; last displayed equality in the proof of Theorem 5.2.3, published p. 120
items.note: Used with L = M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ), free of rank one over R∞(τ_𝒮) by Theorem 5.1.1: j_*j^*(∏p^m M∞(σ^σ)) = j_*j^*(∏p^m R∞(τ_𝒮))·M∞(σ^σ). Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 (route 6).

items.name: Crossing loci pull back along adjunction of formal variables
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian complete local flat 𝒪-algebra with A/ϖ reduced, and let P₁,…,P_n ⊂ A be the preimages of the minimal primes of A/ϖ. Put B = A[[t₁,…,t_h]]. Then the minimal primes of B/ϖ = (A/ϖ)[[t]] are the P_iB/ϖB, and for Z_A := ∪_{i<j} V(P_i + P_j) ⊂ Spec A, its preimage in Spec B is Z_B := ∪_{i<j} V(P_iB + P_jB), the crossing locus of the special fibre of Spec B. Hence U_B := Spec B \ Z_B is the preimage of U_A := Spec A \ Z_A. (All spectra are ordinary spectra of the complete rings.)
items.locator: general; justifies 'j and U come from pulling back j₀' (§5.2, published p. 119) and Remark 5.2.4
items.note: Applied with A = ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ} and B = R∞(τ_𝒮). Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).

items.name: Specializing an ideal-shaped lattice map at an 𝒪-point
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring, π ∈ A, u : M → A an injective A-linear map from a finitely generated module, I = u(M), and suppose π^nA ⊂ I for some n. Let a : A → 𝒪 be a ring map to a discrete valuation ring with a(π) ≠ 0. Then the induced map M ⊗_A 𝒪 → 𝒪 has image I𝒪 ≠ 0 and 𝒪-torsion kernel; hence it identifies M_𝒪^{tf} (D25) with the nonzero ideal I𝒪, which is free of rank one, even when M ⊗_A 𝒪 has torsion.
items.locator: general; clarifies (5.9) in the proof of Theorem 5.3.5, published p. 126
items.note: Applied with A = R∞(τ_𝒮) ≅ M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ), M = M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ), π = p (coker M∞(ι) = M∞(coker ι) is killed by a power of p), a = the point λ. The torsion of M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)/λ maps to zero, so the image of (5.9) is the image of j_*j^*(∏p^m R∞(τ_𝒮)) in 𝒪. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).

items.name: Stalkwise depth ≥ 2 gives a regular sequence of length two in the support ideal
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring, M a finitely generated A-module and I ⊂ A an ideal with depth_{A_P}(M_P) ≥ 2 for every P ∈ V(I) ∩ Supp(M). If IM ≠ M then I contains an M-regular sequence of length two (depth_I(M) ≥ 2); if IM = M, depth_I(M) = ∞ by convention.
items.locator: general; input for [HK04, Prop. 3.5] in Theorem 5.2.3, published p. 120
items.note: Standard: depth_I(M) = min_{P∈V(I)} depth M_P (prime avoidance). Not stated in the paper. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).

items.name: Local cohomology as a colimit of Ext
items.statement: For a commutative ring A, an ideal I ⊂ A and q ∈ ℕ, the local cohomology functor H^q_I on A-modules is M ↦ colim_n Ext^q_A(A/I^n, M).
items.locator: general (mathlib: Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/LocalCohomology.lean, definition localCohomology, commit 082e2d37); background for [HK04, Prop. 3.5] in Theorem 5.2.3
items.note: Not used explicitly by the paper; it enters only through the standard proof of the cited extension statement (T56). Library: localCohomology at the pinned commits.

api.name: use_existing_colimit
api.statement: Import localCohomology rather than define a second module.

api.name: local_cohomology_map
api.statement: Use its functor map for A-linear module maps.

api.name: change_support_radical
api.statement: Use L07 when the defining ideal changes without changing its radical.

items.name: Local cohomology depends only on the radical of the ideal
items.statement: For a Noetherian commutative ring A and ideals I, J ⊂ A with √I = √J, the functors H^q_I and H^q_J are naturally isomorphic for every q.
items.locator: general (mathlib: localCohomology.isoOfSameRadical, commit 082e2d37); background for Theorem 5.2.3
items.note: Needed because Z is given only as a closed subset (V(I) for any I with the right radical). Not used explicitly by the paper. Library: localCohomology.isoOfSameRadical at the pinned commits.

items.name: Modules versus quasi-coherent sheaves on an affine scheme
items.statement: For a commutative ring A, M ↦ M̃ is an equivalence from A-modules to quasi-coherent 𝒪_{Spec A}-modules.
items.locator: general (mathlib: AlgebraicGeometry.tildeEquiv, Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Tilde.lean, commit 082e2d37); used implicitly in §5.2
items.note: The paper passes freely between R∞(τ_𝒮)-modules and quasi-coherent sheaves on X∞(τ_𝒮) (Lemma 5.2.2, Theorem 5.2.3). Library: AlgebraicGeometry.tildeEquiv at the pinned commits.

api.name: module_to_affine_sheaf
api.statement: Use the functor of tildeEquiv for finite modules.

api.name: affine_sections_inverse
api.statement: Use the inverse/global-sections functor and unit.

api.name: transport_maps
api.statement: Transport A-linear maps to sheaf maps using the equivalence.

items.name: Depth, Cohen–Macaulay, maximal Cohen–Macaulay, full support
items.statement: For a Noetherian ring A, an ideal I and a finitely generated A-module M, depth_I(M) is the supremum of the lengths of M-regular sequences in I (= ∞ if IM = M). For A local, depth(M) := depth_𝔪(M). A nonzero finitely generated M over a Noetherian local ring is Cohen–Macaulay if depth(M) = dim Supp(M), and maximal Cohen–Macaulay if depth(M) = dim A. M has full support if Supp(M) = Spec A (for A a domain, maximal Cohen–Macaulay implies full support).
items.locator: general; used in Definition 3.5.1(1),(3), Lemma 5.2.2 ('Cohen–Macaulay of full support') and Theorem 5.2.3 (published pp. 119–120); Stacks 10.103 and 47.11 as given by the earlier checkpoint
items.note: The paper's 'maximally Cohen–Macaulay over R∞(τ_𝒮)' (Def. 3.5.1(1)) and 'Cohen–Macaulay of full support' (Lemma 5.2.2) agree because R∞(τ_𝒮) is a domain. Planned: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3 plans depth, Cohen–Macaulay modules and Auslander–Buchsbaum.

api.name: depth_regular_sequence
api.statement: A regular sequence in I of length n gives depth_I(M)≥n.

api.name: cm_localize
api.statement: Apply T57 to localizations.

api.name: full_support_not_automatic
api.statement: Require full support when replacing dim Supp(M_P) by dim A_P.

items.name: Image of an injective map of line bundles on a regular scheme
items.statement: Let U be a regular Noetherian scheme and f : ℒ₁ → ℒ₂ an injective map of invertible sheaves. Then im f = 𝒪_U(−D)·ℒ₂, where D = Σ_x length_{𝒪_{U,x}}((coker f)_x) · [\overline{{x}}] over the points x of codimension one, and 𝒪_U(−D) = ∏_x 𝓘_x^{n_x} with 𝓘_x the (invertible) ideal sheaf of the prime divisor \overline{{x}}.
items.locator: general; implicit in the proof of Lemma 5.2.2 ('the ideal sheaf of the Cartier divisor corresponding to the cokernel'), published p. 119
items.note: Regular local rings are UFDs (Auslander–Buchsbaum), so height-one primes are locally principal. Standard. Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 (route 6).

items.name: [Bre14, Conjectures B.1 and 1.2] — Dembélé's mod p multiplicity one and Breuil's lattice conjecture (context)
items.statement: §5.3 deduces generalizations of the conjectures of Dembélé (mod p multiplicity one) and Breuil (lattices in completed cohomology depend only on the local Galois representations), [Bre14, Conjectures B.1 and 1.2], stated there for GL₂: Theorem 5.3.4 is the GL₃ mod p multiplicity one statement and Theorem 5.3.5 the GL₃ lattice statement.
items.note: Cited for context only; nothing from [Bre14] is used in the proofs. The paragraph also records that Theorem 5.3.4 follows immediately from Theorem 5.1.1 and that Theorem 5.3.5 needs the image in Theorem 5.2.3 to be an ideal times a free module (which relies on Theorem 5.1.1). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Global setup — CM field and definite unitary group
items.statement: (Setup of [LLHLM18, §7.1].) F/ℚ is a CM field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺ ≠ ℚ; Σ_p⁺ (resp. Σ_p) is the set of places of F⁺ (resp. of F) above p. G/F⁺ is a reductive group which is an outer form of GL₃, quasi-split at all finite places of F⁺, split over F, and definite: G(F⁺_v) ≅ U₃(ℝ) for all v | ∞.
items.note: Definiteness makes G(F⁺)\G(𝔸^∞_{F⁺})/U finite, so the spaces S(U,W) below are finite 𝒪-modules ('algebraic automorphic forms'). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [EGH13, §7.1] — integral model 𝒢 and the isomorphisms ι, ι_w (5.7)
items.statement: G admits a reductive model 𝒢 defined over 𝒪_{F⁺}[1/N], for some N ∈ ℕ prime to p, together with an isomorphism ι : 𝒢_{/𝒪_F[1/N]} ⥲ GL_{3/𝒪_F[1/N]} (5.7), which specializes to ι_w : 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺_v}) ⥲ 𝒢(𝒪_{F_w}) ⥲ GL₃(𝒪_{F_w}) for all places w ∈ Σ_p with w|_{F⁺} = v.
items.note: Cited ('Recall from [EGH13, Section 7.1]'). The ι_ṽ are used to transport K = ∏_{ṽ∈𝒮} GL₃(𝒪_{F_ṽ})-representations to 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})-representations (σ ↦ σ ∘ ∏ι_ṽ), and also at ṽ₁ and at the places of Σ₀⁺. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: S(U, W) — algebraic automorphic forms on the definite unitary group
items.statement: Let U = U^pU_p ≤ G(𝔸^{(∞,p)}_{F⁺}) × 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) be a compact open subgroup and W a finite 𝒪-module endowed with a continuous action of U. Then S(U, W) := {f : G(F⁺)\G(𝔸^∞_{F⁺}) → W | f(gu) = u^{-1}f(g) for all g ∈ G(𝔸^∞_{F⁺}), u ∈ U}.
items.note: 'Finite 𝒪-module' is used in the sense of finitely generated (W is often an 𝒪-lattice such as W_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ σ°). U acts on W through its components at Σ₀⁺ (via ι_ṽ on σ(τ_v)°) and at p. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: S(U^p, W) — forms of tame level U^p and infinite level at p
items.statement: S(U^p, W) := lim→_{U_p} S(U^pU_p, W), where U_p ≤ 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) runs over the compact open neighbourhoods of 1 ∈ 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}).
items.note: For the colimit to make sense W must carry a U^pU_p-action for all U_p (e.g. the p-part acts trivially, W = W_{Σ₀⁺}, as in §5.3.4). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: S̃(U^p, W) — ϖ-adically completed cohomology
items.statement: S̃(U^p, W) := lim←_s S(U^p, W/ϖ^s), with S(U^p, W/ϖ^s) = lim→_{U_p} S(U^pU_p, W/ϖ^s) as in def-S-Up-W.
items.note: Carries commuting actions of 𝕋^univ and of G(F⁺_p) ⊃ 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) ≅ K (via ∏ι_ṽ). Used with W = W_{Σ₀⁺} in §5.3.4 (S̃(U^p,W)[λ], Schikhof dual S̃(U^p,W)^d). Planned: CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.1–CC.2 and CC.8 plan the completed towers and their unitary adapters.

api.name: tower_actions
api.statement: Hecke and local-group actions commute.

api.name: tower_residue
api.statement: Relate finite-level coefficients to the completed tower.

items.name: 𝒫_U and the universal Hecke algebra 𝕋_𝒫
items.statement: For U as above, 𝒫_U is the set of finite places w of F whose restriction v := w|_{F⁺} splits in F and at which U is unramified. For 𝒫 ⊂ 𝒫_U of finite complement, the universal Hecke algebra 𝕋_𝒫 = 𝒪[T_w^{(i)} : w ∈ 𝒫, 0 ≤ i ≤ n] on 𝒫 acts naturally on S(U, W).
items.note: N is not defined in the paper; n = 3 (GL₃) is meant (issue). The T_w^{(i)} are the usual unramified Hecke operators at w (transported via ι_w); their definition is not restated. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The maximal ideal 𝔪 of 𝕋_𝒫 attached to r̄ (Hecke normalisation)
items.statement: Let r̄ : G_F → GL₃(𝔽) be a continuous Galois representation. 𝔪 ⊆ 𝕋_𝒫 is the maximal ideal which is the kernel of the system of Hecke eigenvalues ᾱ : 𝕋_𝒫 → 𝔽 associated with r̄, i.e. ᾱ satisfies det(1 − r̄^∨(Frob_w)X) = Σ_{j=0}^{3} (−1)^j (𝐍_{F/ℚ}(w))^{\binom{j}{2}} ᾱ(T_w^{(j)}) X^j for all w ∈ 𝒫.
items.note: Normalisation: the dual r̄^∨ and the factor 𝐍(w)^{j(j−1)/2}. The same formula (with α, r, λ) defines λ in §5.3.4 and 𝔪̄ in Definition 6.0.1. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: r̄ automorphic (§5.3)
items.statement: r̄ is automorphic if S(U, W)_𝔪 is nonzero for some U and W (as in def-algebraic-automorphic-forms, with 𝒫 ⊂ 𝒫_U).
items.note: Refined in Definition 6.0.1 (automorphic of weight V, level U and coefficients W; W(r̄) ≠ ∅). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [CEG+16, §2.3] — the auxiliary place v₁
items.statement: A place v₁ of F⁺ is chosen 'for technical reasons' as in [CEG+16, Section 2.3].
items.note: Cited; the required properties of v₁ are not restated in this paper. v₁ enters the level (Iwahori-type level at v₁) and 𝕋^univ (operators T_{v₁}^{(j)}). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The fixed tame level U^p
