items.statement: U^p ≤ G(𝔸^{(∞,p)}_{F⁺}) is the subgroup with: (1) (U^p)_v = 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺_v}) for all finite places v of F⁺ which split in F and do not belong to Σ_p⁺ ∪ {v₁}; (2) (U^p)_{v₁} is the preimage of the upper triangular matrices under 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺_{v₁}}) → 𝒢(k_{v₁}) →^{ι_{ṽ₁}} GL₃(k_{ṽ₁}); (3) (U^p)_v is hyperspecial maximal compact in G(F⁺_v) if v is inert in F.
items.note: Places of Σ₀⁺ (split, by split ramification) get maximal level 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺_v}); ramification at Σ₀⁺ is carried by the coefficient module W_{Σ₀⁺}. No finite place ramifies in F/F⁺ by hypothesis (i). In arXiv v3 the places of Σ₀⁺ were excluded from (1). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Σ₀⁺ — ramified places away from p
items.statement: For an automorphic r̄, Σ₀⁺ is the set of finite places of F⁺ which are restrictions of the finite places of F away from p where r̄ ramifies.
items.note: By split ramification (ii) every v ∈ Σ₀⁺ splits in F. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [CHT08, Definition 2.4.14] — minimally ramified lifts and types (as used)
items.statement: For a place ṽ ∤ p of F, the notion of a minimally ramified lift of r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}} ([CHT08, Definition 2.4.14]). As used: for v ∈ Σ₀⁺, τ_ṽ is 'the minimally ramified type in the sense of [CHT08, Definition 2.4.14] corresponding to r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}}' (the inertial type of its minimally ramified lifts), and a characteristic-0 r is minimally ramified at ṽ if r|_{G_{F_ṽ}} is a minimally ramified lift.
items.note: Cited, not restated. That all minimally ramified lifts have one and the same inertial type is implicit in 'the minimally ramified type'. Planned: LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2 plans minimally ramified deformation conditions away from p; LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 plans fixed labeled Hodge-type and inertial-type potentially semistable deformation rings in every rank, with bounded-height lattice moduli and minimally ramified conditions.

items.name: Minimal types σ(τ_v) at Σ₀⁺ and the coefficient lattice W_{Σ₀⁺}
items.statement: For each v ∈ Σ₀⁺ (with a chosen ṽ | v), τ_ṽ is the minimally ramified type corresponding to r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}} and σ(τ_ṽ) is the GL₃(𝒪_{F_ṽ})-representation over E associated with it (cf. the beginning of §5.3.1); σ(τ_v) := σ(τ_ṽ) ∘ ι_ṽ, a 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺_v})-representation independent of the choice of ṽ | v. For each v ∈ Σ₀⁺ fix an 𝒪-lattice σ(τ_v)° ⊂ σ(τ_v), and put W_{Σ₀⁺} := ⊗_{v∈Σ₀⁺} σ(τ_v)°.
items.note: The independence of ṽ is asserted without proof. 'cf. the beginning of §5.3.1' points to Proposition 2.2.6/[CEG+16, Thm 3.7], stated there for tame types at places above p; for ṽ ∤ p the analogous inertial local Langlands types are meant. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: 𝕋^univ, its action on S(U^pU_p, W_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ V), and 𝔪 ⊆ 𝕋^univ
items.statement: 𝕋^univ is the abstract Hecke algebra over 𝒪 generated by formal variables T_w^{(j)}, where w runs over the finite places of F such that w|_{F⁺} is split in F and w|_{F⁺} ∉ Σ₀⁺ ∪ Σ_p⁺ ∪ {v₁}, and by T_{v₁}^{(j)} for j = 1, 2, 3. For a module V over 𝒪 with an action of the p-adic group (printed: 'a G(𝔸^{(∞,p)}_{F⁺})-module V'), 𝕋^univ acts naturally on S(U^pU_p, W), S(U^p, W) and S̃(U^p, W), where W = W_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ V (cf. [CEG+16, §2.3]); 𝔪 ⊆ 𝕋^univ is 'the maximal ideal as before' (kernel of the eigensystem ᾱ of r̄ given by the characteristic-polynomial formula of def-m-rbar).
items.note: Two issues recorded: V must be a 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})- (or U_p-) module, not a G(𝔸^{(∞,p)}_{F⁺})-module; and the formula determines ᾱ only on the T_w^{(j)}, not on T_{v₁}^{(j)}. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Standing assumption: S(U, W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 for some V
items.statement: From this point on it is assumed that S(U, W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 (U = U^pU_p, W = W_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ V) for some choice of V. The paper remarks: 'In fact, one can show, by the proof of Proposition 6.0.2, that this is a consequence of the hypothesis that r̄ is automorphic.'
items.note: This assumption (nonvanishing at the fixed minimal tame level and coefficients) is what makes the patching functor M̃∞ nonzero (cf. §6(11), (16)). The remark's justification needs the hypotheses of Proposition 6.0.2 (split ramification, Taylor–Wiles, automorphy of a reachable weight); recorded as a minor gap. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Global hypotheses (i)–(iv) of §5.3
items.statement: In the remainder of §5.3, r̄ : G_F → GL₃(𝔽) is an automorphic Galois representation that satisfies the Taylor–Wiles conditions of [LLHLM18, Definition 7.3], and furthermore: (i) the extension F/F⁺ is unramified at all finite places; (ii) (split ramification) if r̄ is ramified at a place w of F, then v = w|_{F⁺} splits as ww^c; (iii) p is unramified in F⁺ and all places of F⁺ above p split in F; (iv) r̄|_{G_{F_w}} is semisimple for all w ∈ Σ_p.
items.note: Compared with [LLHLM18], 'p splits completely in F⁺' is relaxed to (iii) (Remark 5.3.2) at the cost of (iv). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: 𝒮, ρ̄_𝒮 and K in the global setting
items.statement: For each v ∈ Σ_p⁺ choose a place ṽ | v of F and let 𝒮 := {ṽ | v ∈ Σ_p⁺}. ρ̄_ṽ := r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}}, ρ̄_𝒮 := (ρ̄_ṽ)_{ṽ∈𝒮}, and K := ∏_{ṽ∈𝒮} GL₃(𝒪_{F_ṽ}).
items.note: By (iii) each F_ṽ/ℚ_p is unramified, so the local results of §§3–5.2 apply to ρ̄_𝒮. ∏ι_ṽ identifies 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) with K. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [LLHLM18, Definition 7.11, Proposition 7.15] — the weak minimal patching functor M̃∞ for r̄
items.statement: M̃∞ is the weak minimal patching functor for r̄ in the sense of [LLHLM18, Definition 7.11], constructed in [LLHLM18, Proposition 7.15]: an exact covariant functor from continuous 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})-representations on finitely generated 𝒪-modules to coherent sheaves on X∞ = Spf R∞, R∞ = ⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^□[[x₁,…,x_h]], built by patching the spaces S(U^pU_p, W_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ −).
items.note: Cited. As corrected in §6: the definition depends on the fixed level U and coefficients W (§6(11)); here U = U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) and W = W_{Σ₀⁺} (§6(14)); its nonvanishing needs Proposition 6.0.2 or the standing assumption (§6(16)); e(M) as in §6(12). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: M∞ := M̃∞ ∘ ∏ι_ṽ — the patching functor for ρ̄_𝒮
items.statement: M∞ := M̃∞ ∘ ∏_{ṽ∈𝒮} ι_ṽ (a K-representation V is sent to M̃∞(V ∘ ∏_ṽ ι_ṽ)), which is a weak minimal patching functor for ρ̄_𝒮 in the sense of Definition 3.5.1 by Proposition 3.5.14.
items.note: With this M∞ all of §§5.1–5.2 (Theorems 5.1.1, 5.2.3) apply. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Ring homomorphism R∞ → 𝕋^univ(W_{Σ₀⁺})_𝔪 and the ideal 𝔪 ⊂ R∞ ([CEG+16, §2.8], [Le18, §4.2], [LLHLM18, §7.3])
items.statement: Along with the construction of M̃∞ (cf. [CEG+16, Section 2.8], [Le18, Section 4.2], [LLHLM18, Section 7.3]) one has a ring homomorphism R∞ = ⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^□[[x₁,…,x_h]] → 𝕋^univ_{U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})}(W_{Σ₀⁺})_𝔪, where 𝕋^univ_{U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})}(W_{Σ₀⁺}) is the image of 𝕋^univ in End_𝒪(S(U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), W_{Σ₀⁺})). 𝔪 also denotes the pullback to R∞ of the maximal ideal of 𝕋^univ_{U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})}(W_{Σ₀⁺})_𝔪.
items.note: Cited. As printed the target is the Hecke algebra of forms of trivial weight at p, which is 0 for 10-generic ρ̄_𝒮 (issue); in effect 𝔪 ⊂ R∞ is the maximal ideal of the local ring R∞, which is all that (5.8) and Theorem 5.3.4 use. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: (5.8) — patched modules mod 𝔪 compute 𝔪-torsion in mod p automorphic forms ([Le18, Theorem 4.1.5])
items.statement: If W̄_{Σ_p⁺} is a smooth finite-dimensional 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})-representation over 𝔽, then (M̃∞(W̄_{Σ_p⁺})/𝔪)^∨ = S(U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), W̄_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ W̄_{Σ_p⁺}^∨)[𝔪], where ·^∨ denotes Pontryagin dual (on the left) and W̄_{Σ₀⁺} = W_{Σ₀⁺}/ϖ.
items.note: Cited 'cf. [Le18, Theorem 4.1.5]'. On the right, W̄_{Σ_p⁺}^∨ is the contragredient and [𝔪] the 𝔪-torsion for 𝕋^univ. Used in Theorems 5.3.3 (W^BM(ρ̄_𝒮) vs W(r̄)) and 5.3.4. In arXiv v3 the '[𝔪]' was missing. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Pontryagin dual
items.statement: For a discrete ϖ-power-torsion 𝒪-module M, M^∨ := Hom_𝒪(M, E/𝒪) (= Hom_𝔽(M, 𝔽) if ϖM = 0, e.g. M finite-dimensional over 𝔽); M^∨∨ ≅ M for M of finite length.
items.note: The symbol ^∨ is also used for contragredients of representations (σ^∨, W̄^∨) and for the dual Galois representation r̄^∨. Planned: CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.3 plans continuous and Pontryagin duals and completed homology.

items.name: σ(τ_ṽ) — the K-type of a tame inertial type (Proposition 2.2.6 as used)
items.statement: For ṽ ∈ 𝒮 and a 1-generic tame inertial type τ_ṽ for I_{F_ṽ}, σ(τ_ṽ) is a smooth GL₃(𝒪_{F_ṽ})-representation over E associated with τ_ṽ as in [CEG+16, Theorem 3.7] ('results towards inertial local Langlands'); σ(τ_𝒮) := ⊗_{ṽ∈𝒮} σ(τ_ṽ). By Proposition 2.2.6, if τ_𝒮 = τ_𝒮(s, μ) with μ − η 1-deep in C₀, the Deligne–Lusztig representation R_s(μ) (inflated to K) is irreducible ([DL76, Thm 6.8]) and σ(τ_𝒮) can be taken to be R_s(μ) ([LLHL19, Cor. 2.3.5]).
items.locator: §5.3.1, first paragraph, published p. 123 (recalling Proposition 2.2.6 and the paragraph before it, published p. 17)
items.note: The text says 'Recall from Proposition 2.2.6 … we defined σ(τ_ṽ)'; the definition is in the paragraph preceding Proposition 2.2.6. σ(τ_ṽ) can be realized over 𝒪 (§3.5); lattices σ(τ_𝒮)^σ with irreducible cosocle σ are unique up to homothety (§4.1.2). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Global/local Langlands normalisation used in Theorem 5.3.1
items.statement: For a regular algebraic conjugate self-dual cuspidal (RACSDC) automorphic representation π of GL₃(𝔸_F) and a fixed isomorphism ι : \overline{ℚ}_p ≅ ℂ, r_ι(π) : G_F → GL₃(\overline{ℚ}_p) denotes the associated Galois representation and r̄_ι(π) its (semisimplified) reduction; 'trivial infinitesimal character' is the weight corresponding to Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0); ⊗_{ṽ∈𝒮} σ(τ_ṽ) is a K-type for ⊗_{ṽ∈𝒮} π_ṽ if Hom_K(⊗_ṽ σ(τ_ṽ), ⊗_ṽ π_ṽ) ≠ 0. Hecke eigenvalues of a characteristic-0 r are normalised by det(1 − r^∨(Frob_w)X) = Σ_{j=0}^3 (−1)^j 𝐍_{F/ℚ}(w)^{\binom{j}{2}} α(T_w^{(j)}) X^j.
items.note: Not defined in this paper; conventions are those of [LLHLM18, §7] (and [CHT08], [EGH13]). The polarization r^c ≅ r^∨ε^{−2} and the Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0) fix the twist. The inertial type of a p-adic Galois representation is read off from its Weil–Deligne representation as in §2 (covariant convention of [CDT99, App. B.1]). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 5.3.1 — automorphy lifting
items.statement: (Global setup of §5.3: F/F⁺, G, 𝒮, K; F/F⁺ unramified at all finite places, p unramified in F⁺, all places above p split in F.) Let r : G_F → GL₃(E) be an absolutely irreducible Galois representation such that (1) for all places w ∈ Σ_p, r̄|_{I_{F_w}} is semisimple and 10-generic; (2) r is unramified almost everywhere and satisfies r^c ≅ r^∨ε^{−2}; (3) for all ṽ ∈ 𝒮, r|_{G_{F_ṽ}} is potentially crystalline, with parallel Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0) and with tame inertial type τ_ṽ ([LLHLM18, Definition 2.1]); (4) r̄ satisfies the Taylor–Wiles conditions as above and r̄ has split ramification; and (5) r̄ ≅ r̄_ι(π) for a RACSDC representation π of GL₃(𝔸_F) with trivial infinitesimal character such that ⊗_{ṽ∈𝒮} σ(τ_ṽ) is a K-type for ⊗_{ṽ∈𝒮} π_ṽ. Then r is automorphic in the sense of [LLHLM18, Section 7.2].
items.note: Proof as printed: 'Given Theorems 5.3.3 and 3.5.3, the proof of [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.4] goes through unchanged' — but by §6(16) that proof was omitted in [LLHLM18] (issue). Theorem 3.5.3 supplies connectedness (irreducibility) of the generic fibre of R^{τ}_{ρ̄} for semisimple 10-generic ρ̄; Theorem 5.3.3 supplies nonvanishing of M∞ on the relevant component. On (1): with 10-genericity, r̄|_{I_{F_w}} semisimple is equivalent to r̄|_{G_{F_w}} semisimple (inflation–restriction, no common inertial constituents), consistent with Remark 5.3.2 and hypothesis (iv). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.4] — automorphy lifting when p splits completely (cited; proof omitted there)
items.statement: [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.4] is the automorphy lifting theorem for potentially crystalline lifts of Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0) and generic tame type under the hypothesis that p splits completely in F⁺ (without semisimplicity at p). Its proof 'was omitted' in [LLHLM18] and uses the same level-lowering techniques ([Tay08]) as Proposition 6.0.2 (§6(16)).
items.note: Cited; Theorem 5.3.1 rests on it. The precise statement of [LLHLM18, Thm 7.4] is not reproduced in this paper; the description above is what Remark 5.3.2 and §6(16) say about it. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 5.3.2 — why semisimplicity at p is assumed
items.statement: Compared to [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.4], Theorem 5.3.1 relaxes the hypothesis that p splits completely to p being unramified, but also assumes that r̄ is semisimple at all places above p, because the connectedness of the generic fibre of R_ρ̄^τ is established here only when ρ̄ is semisimple (it is known for non-semisimple ρ̄ when all shapes have length ≥ 2). A counterpart of [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.4] for non-semisimple representations is announced as work in progress.
items.note: States (without proof here) that the generic fibre of R_ρ̄^τ is connected for non-semisimple ρ̄ when all shapes have length ≥ 2. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: W(r̄) — Serre weights of r̄ at the fixed level (§5.3.2)
items.statement: W(r̄) is the set of irreducible K-representations σ over 𝔽 such that S(U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), W̄_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ (σ^∨ ∘ ∏_{ṽ∈𝒮} ι_ṽ))_𝔪 ≠ 0.
items.note: Depends on the fixed U^p and W_{Σ₀⁺}. Same symbol as, but different from, W(r̄) of Definition 6.0.1 (Serre weights of 𝒢 at arbitrary level and coefficients, no contragredient). By (5.8), W(r̄) = W^BM(ρ̄_𝒮) for M∞ = M̃∞ ∘ ∏ι_ṽ. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 5.3.3 — the weight part of Serre's conjecture
items.statement: (Global setup of §5.3, including the standing nonvanishing assumption.) Let r̄ : G_F → GL₃(𝔽) be a continuous Galois representation satisfying the Taylor–Wiles conditions. Assume that ρ̄_ṽ := r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}} is semisimple and 10-generic for all ṽ ∈ 𝒮, that r̄ is automorphic, and that r̄ has split ramification. Then W(r̄) ∘ ∏_{ṽ∈𝒮} ι_ṽ = W?(ρ̄_𝒮) [as printed; since W(r̄) and W?(ρ̄_𝒮) are both sets of K-representations, the type-correct statement is W(r̄) = W?(ρ̄_𝒮)].
items.note: Proof: W^BM(ρ̄_𝒮) = W(r̄) (printed '= W(r̄) ∘ ∏ι_ṽ') by (5.8), and W^BM(ρ̄_𝒮) = W?(ρ̄_𝒮) by Theorem 3.5.2 (e(M∞(σ)) = 1 iff σ ∈ W?). Correct modulo the notational slip (issue). Previous-pass statement listed the global conventions; replaced by the printed statement. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 5.3.4 — mod p multiplicity one
items.statement: (Global setup of §5.3.) Let τ_𝒮 and σ ∈ W?(ρ̄_𝒮, τ_𝒮) be as in the statement of Theorem 5.1.1 (τ_𝒮 13-generic; σ = F(λ) with λ_{π^{-1}(i)} in alcove C₁ whenever ℓ(w̃*_i) ≤ 1). Then S(U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), (σ̄(τ_𝒮)^σ ∘ ∏_{v∈Σ_p⁺} ι_ṽ)^∨ ⊗_{𝒪_E} W_{Σ₀⁺})[𝔪] is one-dimensional over 𝔽.
items.note: Proof: by (5.8), M∞(σ̄(τ_𝒮)^σ)/𝔪 ≅ M̃∞(σ̄(τ_𝒮)^σ ∘ ∏ι_ṽ)/𝔪 ≅ (S(U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), (σ̄(τ_𝒮)^σ ∘ ∏ι_ṽ)^∨ ⊗_𝒪 W_{Σ₀⁺})[𝔪])^∨, and by Theorem 5.1.1 (M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ) ≅ R∞(τ_𝒮)) its dimension is one. Checked. ⊗_{𝒪_E} W_{Σ₀⁺} of an 𝔽-module is ⊗ W̄_{Σ₀⁺}. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Minimally ramified r (§5.3.4)
items.statement: Let r : G_F → GL₃(E) be an automorphic Galois representation as in Theorem 5.3.1. r is minimally ramified if r|_{G_{F_ṽ}} is minimally ramified in the sense of [CHT08, Definition 2.4.14] for all v ∈ Σ₀⁺.
items.note: Then the inertial type of r at ṽ ∈ Σ₀⁺ is the minimal type τ_ṽ, so the coefficient module W_{Σ₀⁺} matches r. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The Hecke ideal λ of r (and λ ⊂ R∞)
items.statement: Following [LLHLM18, §7.1], λ ⊂ 𝕋^univ is the kernel of the system of Hecke eigenvalues α : 𝕋^univ → 𝒪 associated with r, i.e. α satisfies det(1 − r^∨(Frob_w)X) = Σ_{j=0}^{3} (−1)^j (𝐍_{F/ℚ}(w))^{\binom{j}{2}} α(T_w^{(j)}) X^j for all w as above. By abuse of notation λ also denotes the prime ideal of R∞ corresponding to r (cited-hlm17-thm-5-2-1).
items.note: As with 𝔪, the formula does not specify α(T_{v₁}^{(j)}) (issue). R∞/λ ≅ 𝒪 (λ is an 𝒪-point). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: S̃(U^p, W_{Σ₀⁺})[λ] ≠ 0
items.statement: Set W := W_{Σ₀⁺} (as printed: 'as in Section 5.3.3'). Then S̃(U^p, W)[λ] is nonzero ('By Theorem 5.3.1').
items.note: Needs r minimally ramified (assumed in Theorem 5.3.5, but only in the next sentence here) and the proof, not the statement, of Theorem 5.3.1 (r is a point of Supp M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)°) at the fixed level) or local–global compatibility at Σ₀⁺ and v₁ (issue). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [HLM17, Theorem 5.2.1] — a minimally ramified r gives a prime of R∞
items.statement: Since r is minimally ramified, r corresponds to a prime ideal λ of R∞ (an 𝒪-valued point, compatible with R∞ → 𝕋^univ and with the Hecke ideal λ) as in [HLM17, Theorem 5.2.1].
items.note: Cited. Minimality matters because R∞ = ⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^□[[x₁,…,x_h]] has no local factors at Σ₀⁺: the minimally ramified local conditions there are formally smooth and are absorbed into the variables. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Schikhof dual ·^d and Schikhof duality
items.statement: For a ϖ-adically complete, separated, ϖ-torsion-free 𝒪-module M (e.g. S̃(U^p, W) or S̃(U^p,W)[λ]), M^d := Hom^{cont}_𝒪(M, 𝒪) with its compact topology; for a finite free 𝒪-module L, L^d = Hom_𝒪(L, 𝒪). Schikhof duality: M ↦ M^d is an anti-equivalence between such modules and compact ϖ-torsion-free linear-topological 𝒪-modules, with M^{dd} ≅ M.
items.locator: §5.3.4 and proof of Theorem 5.3.5, published pp. 125–126 (spelled 'Schikhov')
items.note: In the proof only the rank-one case matters: dualizing an inclusion 𝒪 → 𝒪 with image (γ) gives an inclusion with image (γ). Also used: S̃(U^p,W)[λ]^d ≅ (S̃(U^p,W)^d/λ)^{tf} canonically. Planned: CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.3 plans continuous and Pontryagin duals and completed homology.

items.name: The patched module M∞ and M∞(σ°) = Hom_K(M∞, (σ°)^d)^d
items.statement: M∞ (without argument) also denotes the patched module, a finitely generated R∞[[K]]-module with continuous K-action ([CEG+16, §2.8], [Le18, §4.2]), from which the patching functor is recovered by M∞(σ°) = Hom_K(M∞, (σ°)^d)^d for K-stable 𝒪-lattices σ° (continuous homomorphisms; ^d = 𝒪-dual).
items.locator: used in the proof of Theorem 5.3.5 ('Hom_{U_p}(M∞, (σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)^d)^d/λ = M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)/λ'), published pp. 125–126
items.note: Not stated explicitly in the paper; M∞ is used both for the module and the functor. The identification with the functor of [LLHLM18, Prop. 7.15] composed with ∏ι_ṽ is implicit. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [CEG+16, Corollary 2.11] — M∞/λ ≅ S̃(U^p, W)^d/λ
items.statement: With W = W_{Σ₀⁺}: M∞/λ ≅ S̃(U^p, W)^d/λ, K-equivariantly (by (the proof of) [CEG+16, Corollary 2.11]).
items.note: Cited. Left side: M∞ ⊗_{R∞} R∞/λ (λ the prime of R∞); right side: S̃^d ⊗_{𝕋} 𝕋/λ. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The lattice σ(τ)⁰ cut out by completed cohomology
items.statement: σ(τ)⁰ := σ(τ) ∩ S̃(U^p, W)[λ] ⊂ σ(τ) ∩ S̃(U^p, W)[λ] ⊗_𝒪 E ≅ σ(τ), where σ(τ) = σ(τ_𝒮) is embedded K-equivariantly (K acting on S̃ via ∏ι_ṽ) into S̃(U^p, W)[λ] ⊗_𝒪 E.
items.note: Implicit: the σ(τ)-isotypic part of S̃(U^p,W)[λ] ⊗ E is one copy of σ(τ), so the embedding and hence σ(τ)⁰ are unique up to E^×/homothety. This follows from the chain of identifications in the proof (Hom_K(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ, S̃[λ]) ≅ (M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)/λ)^d ≅ 𝒪 by Theorem 5.1.1). The paper writes σ(τ) for σ(τ_𝒮) in the statement. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 5.3.5 — Breuil's lattice conjecture for GL₃
items.statement: (Global setup of §5.3.) Let r : G_F → GL₃(E) be as in Theorem 5.3.1. Assume furthermore that r is minimally ramified. Let {τ_ṽ}_{ṽ∈𝒮} be a 13-generic tame type. The lattice σ(τ)⁰ := σ(τ) ∩ S̃(U^p, W)[λ] ⊂ σ(τ) ∩ S̃(U^p, W)[λ] ⊗_𝒪 E ≅ σ(τ) (W = W_{Σ₀⁺}) depends only on {r|_{G_{F_ṽ}}}_{ṽ∈𝒮}.
items.note: 'Depends only on' means: up to homothety, for the fixed global setup (U^p, W_{Σ₀⁺}); τ_ṽ is necessarily the inertial type of r|_{G_{F_ṽ}} from Theorem 5.3.1(3). Proof: σ(τ_𝒮)⁰ = Σ_κ γ(κ)^{-1}σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ([EGS15, Lemma 4.1.2]); (γ(κ)) is the index of the restriction of Hom's (thm-5-3-5-step-hom-index), transported by Schikhof duality and [CEG+16, Cor. 2.11] to the image of (5.9), which by Theorem 5.2.3 is the image mod λ of j_*j^*(∏p(θ)^{m(θ)}R∞(τ_𝒮)); by Remark 5.2.4 this ideal comes from ⊗̂R_ṽ^□, so its image mod λ depends only on the framed local points {r|_{G_{F_ṽ}}}. Unstated but needed: independence of the framing (the ideal of ⊗̂R^□ is stable under the change-of-frame automorphisms, since the connected framing group preserves each component p(θ) and j₀ is canonical). Previous pass's statement kept, with exact wording. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [EGS15, Lemma 4.1.2] — a lattice is the sum of its saturated cosocle lattices
items.statement: As used: let σ(τ_𝒮) have multiplicity-free reduction, σ(τ_𝒮)⁰ ⊂ σ(τ_𝒮) a K-stable lattice and, for each κ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮)), γ(κ) ∈ 𝒪 with γ(κ)^{-1}σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ⊂ σ(τ_𝒮)⁰ saturated. Then σ(τ_𝒮)⁰ = Σ_{κ∈JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮))} γ(κ)^{-1}σ(τ_𝒮)^κ.
items.note: Cited. Multiplicity-freeness of σ̄(τ_𝒮) holds for 13-generic τ_𝒮 (Theorem 4.1.9). The phrase 'for some γ(κ) ∈ 𝒪' in the paper is redundant (γ(κ) was already defined). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The scalars γ(κ)
items.statement: Fix σ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮)) as in Theorem 5.1.1, a saturated inclusion σ(τ_𝒮)^σ ⊂ σ(τ_𝒮)⁰, and saturated inclusions σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ⊂ σ(τ_𝒮)^σ for all κ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮)). γ(κ) ∈ 𝒪 is chosen so that γ(κ)^{-1}σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ⊂ σ(τ_𝒮)⁰ is saturated (well defined up to 𝒪^×).
items.note: The inclusions σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ⊂ σ(τ_𝒮)^σ are fixed independently of r; only the ideals (γ(κ)) depend on r, and the theorem reduces to showing they depend only on {r|_{G_{F_ṽ}}}. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Index of the restriction of Hom's is (γ(κ)) (step in Theorem 5.3.5)
items.statement: The image of the inclusion (restriction along σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ⊂ σ(τ_𝒮)^σ) 𝒪 ≅ Hom_{U_p}(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ, S̃(U^p,W)[λ]) → Hom_{U_p}(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ, S̃(U^p,W)[λ]) ≅ 𝒪 is given by the ideal (γ(κ)). [Hom_{U_p} as printed; K = 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) is meant.]
items.note: Checked: with ι₀ the embedding defining σ(τ_𝒮)⁰, Hom_K(σ^σ, S̃[λ]) = 𝒪·ι₀|_{σ^σ} (σ^σ ⊂ σ⁰ saturated) and Hom_K(σ^κ, S̃[λ]) = γ(κ)^{-1}𝒪·ι₀|_{σ^κ}, so the restriction has index (γ(κ)). The rank-one statements Hom ≅ 𝒪 are justified a posteriori by the duality chain and Theorem 5.1.1. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Transport of (γ(κ)) to the patched module (step in Theorem 5.3.5)
items.statement: (a) By Schikhof duality the natural inclusion 𝒪 ≅ Hom_{U_p}((S̃(U^p,W)[λ])^d, (σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)^d) → Hom_{U_p}((S̃(U^p,W)[λ])^d, (σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)^d) ≅ 𝒪, and its 𝒪-dual Hom_{U_p}((S̃[λ])^d, (σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)^d)^d → Hom_{U_p}((S̃[λ])^d, (σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)^d)^d, are given by the ideal (γ(κ)). (b) S̃(U^p,W)[λ]^d is canonically isomorphic to the torsion-free part of S̃(U^p,W)^d/λ. (c) Hence, using M∞/λ ≅ S̃(U^p,W)^d/λ, (γ(κ)) gives the inclusion Hom_{U_p}(M∞/λ, (σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)^d)^d → Hom_{U_p}(M∞/λ, (σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)^d)^d. (d) Hom_{U_p}(M∞/λ, (σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)^d)^d is isomorphic to (the p-torsion-free part of) Hom_{U_p}(M∞, (σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)^d)^d/λ = M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)/λ, and similarly for κ.
items.note: Checked: Hom_K(M∞/λ, V^d) = Hom_K(M∞, V^d)[λ] = (M∞(V)^d)[λ], whose 𝒪-dual is (M∞(V)/λ)^{tf}. Uses def-schikhof-dual, def-patched-module-and-functor, cited-ceg16-cor-2-11. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: (5.9) — the index (γ(κ)) is the specialization of the gauge ideal
items.statement: The image of (5.9) 𝒪 ≅ M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)/λ → M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)/λ ≅ 𝒪 is given by the ideal (γ(κ)). On the other hand, by Theorem 5.2.3 the image of (5.9) is (j_*j^*(∏_{θ∈W?(ρ̄_𝒮)} p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮)))·(M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)/λ). Hence (γ(κ)) is generated by (the images of) elements of the ideal j_*j^*(∏_{θ∈W?(ρ̄_𝒮)} p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮)) modulo λ.
items.note: The left isomorphism 𝒪 ≅ M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)/λ holds only for the torsion-free quotient (D25; issue); the image is unaffected because the torsion maps to zero in M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)/λ ≅ R∞(τ_𝒮)/λ = 𝒪 (T63). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 5.3.6 — explicit description of σ(τ)⁰ for shapes of length ≥ 2 ([Le18, Theorem 14])
items.statement: In the hypotheses of Theorem 5.3.5, assume further that w̃(ρ̄_ṽ, τ_ṽ)_i has length at least 2 for all ṽ ∈ 𝒮 and i ∈ ℤ/f_ṽ. Then the lattice σ(τ)⁰ can be described explicitly as in [Le18, Theorem 14].
items.note: Cited, no proof. The theorem number 'Theorem 14' is in a different numbering style from the '[Le18, Theorem 4.1.5]' cited on p. 123; not checked against Le18. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: §6(1) — meaning of 'special fibre as predicted by geometric Breuil–Mézard' in [LLHLM18, Theorem 1.1]
items.statement: Under the assumptions of [LLHLM18, Theorem 1.1], the special fibre of R_ρ̄^{(2,1,0),τ} is reduced and the number of its irreducible components is less than or equal to #(W?(ρ̄^{ss}) ∩ JH(σ̄(τ))), with equality if ρ̄ is semisimple.
items.note: Stated as a clarification of [LLHLM18, Thm 1.1]; 'can be checked directly using Theorem 6.14, Tables 3, 7, 8, Propositions 8.5, 8.6, and 8.12, and the results of Section 8.2.2' of [LLHLM18]. Not proved here. Recorded also as E101. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: §6(11) — weak minimal patching functor at a fixed level and coefficients
items.statement: In [LLHLM18, Definition 7.11(2)], 'automorphic of weight V' is replaced by 'automorphic of weight V, level U, and coefficients W', where U is a fixed compact open subgroup of G(𝔸^{∞,p}_F) × 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) [sic; 𝔸_{F⁺} meant] which is unramified at places v | p, and W is a fixed 𝒪-module with a U-action on which the factor 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) acts trivially. The definition of patching functor depends on these implicit choices of U and W.
items.note: This is the notion used for M̃∞ in §5.3 (U = U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), W = W_{Σ₀⁺}). Recorded also as E111. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: §6(12) — corrected definition of e(M)
items.statement: Given a finitely generated R∞-module M with scheme-theoretic support Spec A of dimension at most d, e(M) is d! times the coefficient of the degree-d term of the Hilbert polynomial of M (considered as an A-module).
items.note: Identical to the definition used in §3.5 of this paper (p. 38): e(M) is the Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity when dim A = d and 0 otherwise. Used in Theorem 3.5.2 and hence Lemma 5.2.2 / Theorem 5.3.3. Recorded also as E112. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).

items.name: Definition 6.0.1 — automorphic of weight V, level U and coefficients W; W(r̄)
items.statement: Let r̄ : G_F → GL₃(𝔽) be a continuous Galois representation. Let V be a Serre weight for 𝒢, U a compact open subgroup of G(𝔸^{∞,p}_F) × 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) [sic; 𝔸_{F⁺}] which is unramified at places v | p, and W an 𝒪-module with a U-action for which the factor 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) acts trivially. r̄ is automorphic of weight V, level U and coefficients W if there exists a cofinite subset 𝒫 ⊂ 𝒫_U such that S(U, V ⊗ W)_{𝔪̄} ≠ 0, where 𝔪̄ is the kernel of the system of Hecke eigenvalues ᾱ : 𝕋_𝒫 → 𝔽 associated with r̄, and ᾱ satisfies det(1 − r̄^∨(Frob_w)X) = Σ_{j=0}^{3} (−1)^j (𝐍_{F/ℚ}(w))^{\binom{j}{2}} ᾱ(T_w^{(j)}) X^j for all w ∈ 𝒫. r̄ is automorphic of weight V (V is a Serre weight of r̄) if r̄ is automorphic of weight V, level U and coefficients W for some U and W as above. W(r̄) is the set of all Serre weights of r̄, and r̄ is automorphic if W(r̄) ≠ ∅.
items.note: Addendum to [LLHLM18, Definition 7.1]. Different from the W(r̄) of §5.3.2 (fixed level and coefficients, contragredient, K-representations). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Proposition 6.0.2 — level lowering to the minimal level and coefficients
items.statement: (Setting of [LLHLM18, §7].) Let r̄ : G_F → GL₃(𝔽) be a continuous Galois representation with split ramification outside p, which is automorphic and satisfies the Taylor–Wiles conditions. If r̄ is automorphic of a reachable weight, then it is automorphic of a reachable weight and level U and coefficients W, where U = ∏_{v∤∞} U_v with U_v = 𝒢(𝒪_v) for v which split in F except for v₁; U_{v₁} the preimage of the upper triangular matrices under 𝒢(𝒪_{v₁}) → 𝒢(k_{v₁}) ⥲_{ι_{ṽ₁}} GL₃(k_{ṽ₁}); U_v a hyperspecial maximal compact open subgroup of G(F_v) if v is inert in F; and W is an 𝒪-lattice in ⊗_{v∈Σ₀⁺} σ(τ_ṽ) ∘ ι_ṽ.
items.note: Proof (sketch as printed): pick tame types τ_v (v | p) with ρ̄_v admissible for τ_v, ℓ(w(ρ̄_v,τ_v)) ≥ 3, V_ṽ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_v)); then S(U, σ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 for a lattice σ in ⊗_v σ(τ_v)∘ι_ṽ; [EGH13, Lemma 7.1.6, Thm 7.2.1] gives r̄ ≅ reduction of r_π; choose a solvable totally real L⁺/F⁺ (prop-6-0-2-choice-L-plus); R_τ^univ is finite over 𝒪_E by the proof of [Gee11, Thm 5.1.4] (with [Gue11, Thm 3.4] and geometric integrality from [LLHLM18, §5.3]); this yields a minimally ramified potentially crystalline lift r, automorphic over L, hence (solvable base change) over F; local–global compatibility gives S(U, σ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 at the minimal level, hence S(U, V′ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 for some reachable V′ ∈ JH(σ̄). Issues: Σ₀⁺ misprinted for Σ_p⁺; existence of a lift from finiteness needs dim R_τ^univ ≥ 1. 'Level-lowering result based on techniques in [Tay08]'. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Reachable Serre weight ([LLHLM18]; as used)
items.statement: 'Reachable' Serre weights are those of [LLHLM18] (the definition is not restated in this paper). As used in the proof of Proposition 6.0.2: if V = ⊗_v V_v (V_v = V_ṽ ∘ ι_ṽ) is reachable, then for each v | p there is a tame type τ_v such that ρ̄_v is admissible with respect to τ_v, ℓ(w(ρ̄_v, τ_v)) ≥ 3, and V_ṽ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_v)); and the proof concludes that some reachable V′ ∈ JH(σ̄) (σ a lattice in ⊗_v σ(τ_v) ∘ ι_ṽ) has S(U, V′ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0.
items.locator: §6(16), Proposition 6.0.2 and its proof, published pp. 130–132
items.note: Cited notion; the reading could not consult [LLHLM18] to state the definition. The last step of the proof needs that the Jordan–Hölder factors of σ̄ contributing to S(U, σ̄ ⊗ W̄)_𝔪 include a reachable one, which presumably follows from the definition. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [LLHLM18] — admissibility of ρ̄ for τ and the shape w(ρ̄, τ) (as used)
items.statement: For ρ̄_v (the restriction of r̄ to the decomposition group at ṽ, v | p) and a tame inertial type τ_v, '[ρ̄_v] is admissible with respect to τ_v' and the shape w(ρ̄_v, τ_v) (an element of the admissible set with length ℓ(w(ρ̄_v, τ_v))) are as in [LLHLM18]; Proposition 6.0.2 uses types with ℓ(w(ρ̄_v, τ_v)) ≥ 3.
items.note: Cited. The choice ℓ ≥ 3 is presumably what makes [LLHLM18, §5.3] (geometric integrality of R^{□,τ_ṽ}) applicable later in the proof; not checked against [LLHLM18]. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [EGH13, Lemma 7.1.6 and Theorem 7.2.1] — automorphic r̄ lifts to r_π
items.statement: If S(U, σ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 (σ a lattice in a type, W coefficients), then r̄ ⊗_𝔽 \overline{𝔽}_p is isomorphic to the reduction of r_π : G_F → GL_n(\overline{ℚ}_p) for some π as in [EGH13, Theorem 7.2.1] (n = 3).
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Base change and solvable descent of automorphy (as used)
items.statement: (a) π_F, the regular algebraic (conjugate) self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) obtained from π by base change; π_L, the base change of π_F to L. (b) 'Solvable base change': if r|_{G_L} is automorphic and L/F is a solvable Galois extension (here L = L⁺F with L⁺/F⁺ solvable Galois, L linearly disjoint from \overline{F}^{ker r̄}(ζ_p)), then r is automorphic.
items.note: Cited without references in the text (standard: base change from unitary groups to GL_n, and Arthur–Clozel solvable descent as used in [CHT08], [Tay08]). Planned: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.5 plans base change and solvable descent of automorphy.

items.name: The auxiliary totally real field L⁺ (proof of Proposition 6.0.2)
items.statement: Choose a totally real extension L⁺ of F⁺ such that: 4 | [L⁺ : ℚ]; L⁺/F⁺ is Galois and solvable; L := L⁺F is linearly disjoint from \overline{F}^{ker r̄}(ζ_p) over F; L/L⁺ is everywhere unramified; p is unramified in L⁺; v₁ splits completely in L; and if π_L is the base change of π_F to L and w is a place of L above ṽ for v ∈ Σ₀⁺, then π_{L,w} has Iwahori fixed vectors and τ_v|_{I_{L_w}} is trivial.
items.note: Existence asserted without argument (standard). Here τ_v for v ∈ Σ₀⁺ is the minimal type at ṽ, while the same letter τ_v was just used for the chosen tame types at v | p. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The deformation rings R_τ^univ and R_𝒮^univ (proof of Proposition 6.0.2)
items.statement: Let S := {v₁} ∪ Σ⁺ and S̃ := {ṽ₁} ∪ {ṽ : v ∈ Σ⁺}; S_L (resp. S̃_L) the places of L⁺ (resp. L) above S (resp. S̃); Σ̃_{L,p}, Σ̃_{L,0}, Σ̃_{L,1} the places of L above Σ̃_p⁺, Σ̃₀⁺ and ṽ₁; Σ̃_L := Σ̃_{L,p} ∪ Σ̃_{L,0}. For ṽ ∈ Σ̃_{L,p}, τ_ṽ := τ_{ṽ|_{F⁺}}|_{I_L}; for ṽ ∈ Σ̃_{L,0}, R^{□,τ_ṽ} is the lifting ring of r̄|_{G_{L_ṽ}} parametrizing lifts whose characteristic polynomial is (X − 1)³. R_τ^univ is the universal deformation ring of the deformation problem (F/F⁺, S, S̃, 𝒪_E, r̄, ε^{−2}δ_{F/F⁺}, {R^□_{ṽ₁}} ∪ {R_ṽ^{□,τ_ṽ}}_{v∈Σ⁺}), and R_𝒮^univ that of (L/L⁺, S_L, S̃_L, 𝒪_E, r̄|_{G_L}, ε^{−2}δ_{L/L⁺}, {R^□_{ũ₁}}_{ũ₁∈S̃_{L,1}} ∪ {R_ṽ^{□,τ_ṽ}}_{ṽ∈Σ̃_L}) — analogues of those of [Gee11, §5].
items.note: Deformation problems in the sense of [CHT08] (polarized by ε^{−2}δ, δ the quadratic character of F/F⁺ or L/L⁺). Notation not defined in the paper: Σ⁺ (presumably Σ_p⁺ ∪ Σ₀⁺), Σ̃_p⁺, Σ̃₀⁺; 'characteristic polynomial is (X − 1)³' refers to the inertia action (unipotent lifts); at v ∈ Σ₀⁺ over F, R_ṽ^{□,τ_ṽ} is not separately defined. S here clashes with the set 𝒮 of §5.3. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [Gee11, Theorem 5.1.4] (proof) — R_τ^univ is finite over 𝒪_E
items.statement: The proof of [Gee11, Theorem 5.1.4] shows that R_τ^univ is finite over 𝒪_E: R_τ^univ is finite over R_𝒮^univ, and R_𝒮^univ is finite over 𝒪_E since (R_𝒮^univ)^{red} is isomorphic to an appropriate Hecke algebra, with the Fontaine–Laffaille deformation rings of [Gee11] replaced by R^{□,τ_ṽ} for ṽ ∈ Σ̃_{L,p}.
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [Gue11, Theorem 3.4] (proof) — (R_𝒮^univ)^red is a Hecke algebra
items.statement: (R_𝒮^univ)^{red} is isomorphic to an appropriate Hecke algebra, by the proof of [Gue11, Theorem 3.4] (with the local deformation rings R^{□,τ_ṽ} at ṽ ∈ Σ̃_{L,p}).
items.note: Cited. Needs the local rings at p to be geometrically integral (cited-llhlm18-geometric-integrality). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [LLHLM18, §5.3] — geometric integrality of R^{□,τ_ṽ}
items.statement: For ṽ ∈ Σ̃_{L,p}, the potentially crystalline lifting ring R^{□,τ_ṽ} (Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0), type τ_ṽ, shape of length ≥ 3) is geometrically integral ([LLHLM18, Section 5.3]).
items.note: Cited. L_ṽ/ℚ_p is unramified (p unramified in L⁺, L/L⁺ unramified) but need not be ℚ_p; the intro of this paper indicates [LLHLM18] treats unramified K for shapes all of whose components have length > 1 (published p. 34: nontriviality from [LLHLM18, Table 7]; only the short shapes needed K = ℚ_p), so the citation plausibly covers this case; not checked against [LLHLM18]. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Existence and automorphy of a minimally ramified lift (step in Proposition 6.0.2)
items.statement: That R_τ^univ is finite over 𝒪_E implies that there is a conjugate self-dual lift r : G_F → GL₃(\overline{ℚ}_p) of r̄ which is minimally ramified outside p and potentially crystalline of type ((0,1,2), τ_v) at ṽ for each v ∈ Σ₀⁺ [sic: Σ_p⁺]. The restriction r|_{G_L}, which corresponds to a point of Spec R_𝒮^univ, is automorphic; solvable base change implies r is automorphic; local–global compatibility implies S(U, σ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 for U and W as in Proposition 6.0.2; then S(U, V′ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 for some reachable V′ ∈ JH(σ̄).
items.note: Two issues: Σ₀⁺ should be Σ_p⁺; and finiteness over 𝒪_E gives a \overline{ℚ}_p-point only together with the lower bound dim R_τ^univ ≥ 1 (standard, part of the proof of [Gee11, Thm 5.1.4]). 'Automorphic' for r|_{G_L} follows from (R_𝒮^univ)^{red} ≅ 𝕋. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Local–global compatibility (as used in Proposition 6.0.2 and §5.3.4)
items.statement: For an automorphic r with the relevant local properties: at v | p, potentially crystalline of type τ_v (Hodge–Tate weights (0,1,2)) implies that the corresponding local component contains σ(τ_v); at v ∈ Σ₀⁺, minimal ramification implies it contains σ(τ_ṽ). Consequently S(U, σ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 at the minimal level U and coefficients W.
items.note: Cited without reference. Planned: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.6 plans local–global compatibility at p.

items.name: §6(16) — consequence for [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.8]
items.statement: Proposition 6.0.2 shows that M∞(⊗_{v∈Σ_p⁺} σ̄(τ_v)°) is nonzero in the third paragraph of the proof of [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.8] (one cannot directly cite [LLHLM18, Definition 7.11(2)] because of the change in §6(11)).

items.name: Local-cohomology restriction exact sequence
items.statement: For Noetherian A, ideal I, U=Spec A minus V(I), and A-module M, the Ext-colimit local cohomology of L06 fits functorially into 0→H_I^0(M)→M→Sec_U(M)→H_I^1(M)→0.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Compare the Ext colimit with derived I-power torsion using an injective resolution and exact filtered colimits. For Noetherian A this agrees with support cohomology (0955). The augmented finite localization Čech complex computes that support functor (0952/0A6T). Its first two cohomology groups are the kernel and cokernel of M→Sec_U(M). The Noetherian comparison is essential, not a theorem already provided by L06. Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 (route 7).
